123	/* HEO scaler factor is 12.20 fixed-point: factor = (src / dst) << 20; 1.0 = 1:1. */
124	static uint32_t scaler_factor(uint32_t src, uint32_t dst)
125	{
126	    if (dst == 0u) { return 0x100000u; }
127	    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)src << 20) / dst);

135	static void heo_bind(uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h,
136	                     uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
137	{

143	        return;
144	    }

147	    Video_GetFrameInfo(&fi);
148	    uint32_t addr = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)fi.buffer;
149	
150	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
151	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, false);
152	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, addr, false);
153	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, 0u, false);
154	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, false);
155	
156	    /* Display rect (HEOCFG3) and source-memory rect (HEOCFG4): equal for 1:1, differ
157	     * when scaling. Written directly — XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize sets both equal. */
158	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG3 = LCDC_HEOCFG3_XSIZE(dst_w - 1u) | LCDC_HEOCFG3_YSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
159	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG4 = LCDC_HEOCFG4_XMEMSIZE(src_w - 1u) | LCDC_HEOCFG4_YMEMSIZE(src_h - 1u);
160	
161	    bool scaling = (dst_w != src_w) || (dst_h != src_h);
162	    if (scaling)
163	    {
164	        uint32_t hf = scaler_factor(src_w, dst_w);
165	        uint32_t vf = scaler_factor(src_h, dst_h);
166	
167	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(1) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(1)

179	    else

182	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(0) | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(0);

195	/* Disable HEO output. The BASE discard is dropped (or handed to the dialog rect)
196	 * by base_discard_reconcile, which owns DISCEN. */
197	static void heo_unbind(void)
198	{
199	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
200	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);

203	/* ── BASE DMA-discard (single DISCEN owner, video-task ctx) ───────────────────
204	 * The LCDC has one BASE discard window (§44.6.4.7): BASE skips its DDR read where
205	 * an opaque layer fully covers it, freeing read bandwidth. base_discard_reconcile
206	 * picks the region each tick — the video rect while HEO is bound, else the dialog
207	 * rect while the song-select modal is open, else none — and applies only on change
208	 * so it isn't re-committing BASE every tick. Keeping every DISCEN write here (never
209	 * in heo_bind/heo_unbind or the UI task) keeps BASE single-writer. */
210	static struct { bool on; uint32_t x, y, w, h; } s_base_disc;
211	
212	static void base_discard_apply(bool on, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t w, uint32_t h)
213	{
214	    if (on == s_base_disc.on && x == s_base_disc.x && y == s_base_disc.y &&
215	        w == s_base_disc.w && h == s_base_disc.h) { return; }
216	
217	    if (on)
218	    {
219	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG5 = LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCXPOS(x) | LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCYPOS(y);
220	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG6 = LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCXSIZE(w - 1u) | LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCYSIZE(h - 1u);
221	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 |= LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
222	    }
223	    else
224	    {
225	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 &= ~LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
226	    }
227	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);   /* commit the CFG change */
228	
229	    s_base_disc.on = on;
230	    s_base_disc.x = x; s_base_disc.y = y; s_base_disc.w = w; s_base_disc.h = h;
231	}
232	
233	static void base_discard_reconcile(void)
234	{
235	    if (s_video_bound)
236	    {
237	        rect_t r = s_video_win;
238	        base_discard_apply(true, r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h);
239	    }
240	    else if (s_dialog_discard)
241	    {
242	        base_discard_apply(true, DIALOG_X, DIALOG_Y, DIALOG_W, DIALOG_H);
243	    }
244	    else
245	    {
246	        base_discard_apply(false, 0u, 0u, 0u, 0u);
247	    }
248	}

250	/* video-task tick: converge HEO to intent + source. Bind on first show, window
251	 * change (rebind flag), or source-size change; unbind when hidden. */
252	static void heo_reconcile(bool source_valid, uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h)
253	{
254	    rect_t w = s_video_win;
255	    bool   win_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
256	    bool   want = s_video_shown && source_valid && win_valid;
257	
258	    if (want && (!s_video_bound || s_video_rebind ||
259	                 src_w != s_bound_src_w || src_h != s_bound_src_h))
260	    {
261	        heo_bind(src_w, src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
262	        s_video_bound  = true;
263	        s_video_rebind = false;
264	    }
265	    else if (!want && s_video_bound)
266	    {
267	        heo_unbind();
268	        s_video_bound = false;
269	    }
270	
271	    /* Own the single BASE discard window (video rect / dialog rect / none). Runs
272	     * after the HEO decision above so it sees the current s_video_bound. */
273	    base_discard_reconcile();
274	}

276	/* ISC IRQ: point HEO at the just-completed ring slot every frame so it always scans
277	 * the freshest complete frame (not a slot the capture engine is mid-write on). This
278	 * is unconditional: writing the layer address while HEO is disabled (video hidden)
279	 * is harmless, and keeping the write out of any task/IRQ-shared flag guarantees the
280	 * scanout base advances regardless of task timing. Latches at the next vsync. */
281	static void heo_frame_latch(uint32_t buffer_addr)
282	{
283	    /* Non-blocking base update: write the HEO frame address and *request* the layer
284	     * attribute update, but do NOT wait for the sync. XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(...,true)
285	     * → XLCDC_UpdateLayerAttributes busy-waits on LCDC_ATTRE/ATTRS_SIP until the update
286	     * latches (a vsync away while HEO scans) — too costly for this per-frame ISC IRQ.
287	     * The address register is double-buffered, so the hardware latches the new base at
288	     * the next vsync on its own; the following frame writes the newer address. OR into
289	     * ATTRE so a pending BASE/OVR update isn't cleared. */
290	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEO[0].LCDC_HEOYFBA = buffer_addr;
291	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_ATTRE |= LCDC_ATTRE_HEO_Msk;
292	}

314	/* Route input for the song-select modal via the layer-screens' background panels.
315	 * Legato treats every layer-screen as stacked and pickable regardless of canvas
316	 * visibility, so a hidden overlay still captures touches meant for the dashboard
317	 * beneath it unless its background panel is disabled (the MGS layer-screen
318	 * "background panel" pattern). PANEL_SONG_SELECT (layer 2) and
319	 * PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART (layer 3) are the first pickable widgets on their
320	 * IGNOREPICK roots, i.e. the layers' background panels. `on` = dialog shown:
321	 * enable the dialog panels and *disable the dashboard* (PANEL_DASHBOARD, layer 0) so
322	 * it's a true modal — nothing behind the dialog (header tap, hamburger) reacts.
323	 * Inverted while closed: dashboard live, overlays pass input through. */
324	/* Gate a panel's whole subtree from picking without repainting it. leWidget's
325	 * setEnabled toggles LE_WIDGET_ENABLED but also invalidates, which would repaint
326	 * an unchanged surface and stall touch (Legato defers input while drawing). We
327	 * only want the pick effect — leUtils_PickFromWidget descends only into ENABLED
328	 * children, and the renderer never reads ENABLED — so toggle the flag directly.
329	 * IGNOREPICK would not do: it stops the panel being the pick result but still lets
330	 * its children be picked, so the subtree wouldn't be gated. */
331	static void panel_set_pickable(leWidget *w, leBool on)
332	{
333	    if (on) { w->flags |=  LE_WIDGET_ENABLED; }

385	/* Set the backlight brightness (0–100%, clamped). The backlight is PWM-dimmed on
386	 * PC18 (PWM channel 0, configured by MCC), period read at runtime so this tracks
387	 * whatever MCC sets. The channel is CPOL_LOW — it idles low (dark) when stopped,
388	 * so the panel stays off until the splash — which means CDTY is the LOW-level
389	 * time and brightness is the high fraction: CDTY = period·(100−pct)/100, so
390	 * pct=100 → CDTY 0 → full bright, pct=0 → CDTY period → off. PWM_ChannelDutySet
391	 * writes CDTY directly while stopped and the update register once running, so
392	 * this is valid both before the channel starts and at runtime. */
393	void UiManager_SetBacklight(uint32_t pct)
394	{
395	    if (pct > 100u) { pct = 100u; }
396	    s_backlight_pct = pct;
397	    uint32_t period = PWM_ChannelPeriodGet(PWM_CHANNEL_0);
398	    PWM_ChannelDutySet(PWM_CHANNEL_0, (period * (100u - pct)) / 100u);
399	}
400	
401	uint32_t UiManager_GetBacklight(void)
402	{
403	    return s_backlight_pct;
404	}
405	
406	/* Light the backlight at the persisted brightness (Settings_Get loads the QSPI
407	 * ring on first use, or the compiled default if no record). The PWM channel is
408	 * stopped (no output) until started here, so the panel stays dark until the
409	 * splash is up — no pre-splash frame. PWM_Initialize ran at startup; this sets
410	 * the duty (while stopped, so the channel starts straight at the target) and
411	 * starts it. */
412	static void enable_backlight(void)
413	{
414	    UiManager_SetBacklight(Settings_Get()->backlight_pct);
415	    PWM_ChannelsStart(PWM_CHANNEL_0_MASK);
416	}
417	
418	/* ── Legato render serialization ──────────────────────────────────────────────
419	 * leAddRootWidget/leRemoveRootWidget mutate Legato's per-layer root lists with no
420	 * locking, and LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks (both run from scheduler start)
421	 * traverse those lists. The boot task edits the scene graph post-scheduler, so it
422	 * suspends those two readers around the edits. Safe to suspend here: at guard
423	 * time no app roots are attached (the splash is pure LCDC scanout), so the
424	 * renderer is idle; resuming hands rendering back. GFX_CANVAS_Tasks is left
425	 * running (it commits canvases; not a root-list reader). */
426	static TaskHandle_t s_legato_task;
427	static TaskHandle_t s_input_task;
428	
429	static void scene_edit_begin(void)
430	{
431	    s_legato_task = xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks");
432	    s_input_task  = xTaskGetHandle("SYS_INPUT_Tasks");
433	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_legato_task); }
434	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_input_task);  }
435	    if (s_legato_task == NULL || s_input_task == NULL)
436	    {
437	        LOG_WARN("UI: render task handle not found; scene edit unguarded\r\n");
438	    }
439	}
440	
441	static void scene_edit_end(void)
442	{
443	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_input_task);  }
444	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_legato_task); }
445	}
446	
447	/* Build the Marvin master screen and run per-panel setup. screenInit_Marvin builds
448	 * all layer-screens and places each on its own Legato layer/canvas (dashboard 0,
449	 * navigation 1, song-select 2) — no re-hosting. Each panel module's *_Setup() then sets
450	 * its canvas window and wires its content/events. */
451	static void init_screens(void)
452	{
453	    /* screenInit_Marvin only flips the one-time "initialized" flag; the widget
454	     * tree (all three layers) is constructed in screenShow_Marvin, which also
455	     * attaches each layer's root to its Legato layer (leAddRootWidget rootN, N). */
456	    (void)screenInit_Marvin();
457	    (void)screenShow_Marvin();
458	
459	    /* The album-art layer (3) must be RGBA8888: the 2D engine has no RGB888 support
460	     * (gfx2dFormats[RGB_888] = -1), so a 24bpp canvas can't be GFX2D-blitted and
461	     * renders garbage. MGS currently emits LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888 for this layer;
462	     * override it here to match the RGBA8888 canvas surface + OVR2 scanout. (Set the
463	     * layer-screen to RGBA8888 in MGS to make this override redundant.) */
464	    leSetLayerColorMode(CANVAS_ALBUM_ART, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888);
465	
466	    ScreenDashboard_Setup();
467	    ScreenNavigation_Setup();
468	    ScreenSongSelect_Setup();
469	    ScreenAlbumArt_Setup();
470	
471	    /* Song-select starts closed: disable its layer-screens' background panels so
472	     * those (hidden) overlays don't capture touches meant for the dashboard.
473	     * UiManager_OpenSongSelect re-enables them. */
474	    songsel_set_input(LE_FALSE);
475	}
476	
477	/* Paint every layer-screen surface once, behind the splash. Legato renders into a
478	 * canvas surface independent of whether that canvas is shown or bound to a hardware
479	 * layer, so a full paint here leaves every surface complete — after which showing a
480	 * screen is a pure layer bind with no repaint. Each panel is VISIBLE by now (its
481	 * *_Setup set it) and its canvas window is full-surface sized, so one invalidate
482	 * lands the whole surface; wait_render_idle then confirms it drained. Relied upon so
483	 * the drawer/dialog need never invalidate on open — MGS builds the nav panel
484	 * setVisible(FALSE), so its boot root-damage paints nothing until this runs. */
485	static void paint_all_screens_once(void)
486	{
487	    Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD);
488	    Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION);
489	    Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT);
490	    Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART->fn->invalidate(Marvin_PANEL_SONG_SELECT_ALBUM_ART);
491	}
492	
493	/* Block until the Legato render task has painted all pending damage. We don't
494	 * drive leUpdate — LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task render correctly when they run;
495	 * we just yield and poll the public idle flag, requiring it to hold continuously
496	 * (a lone idle sample is an inter-frame gap, not a finished paint). Bounded. */
497	static void wait_render_idle(void)
498	{
499	    TickType_t deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
500	    TickType_t idle_since = 0;
501	    bool       idle_run   = false;
502	
503	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
504	    {
505	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
506	        {
507	            if (!idle_run)
508	            {
509	                idle_run   = true;
510	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
511	            }
512	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
513	            {
514	                return;
515	            }
516	        }
517	        else
518	        {
519	            idle_run = false;
520	        }
521	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
522	    }
523	    LOG_WARN("UI: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
524	}
525	
526	/* ── boot sequence ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
527	
528	static void ui_boot_task(void *param)
529	{
530	    (void)param;
531	
532	    /* PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work, as fast as the SD allows. */
533	    (void)ScreenSplash_Load();   /* loads the image, or fills the fallback colour */
534	    ScreenSplash_Show(xlcdc_layer(SPLASH_HW_LAYER));
535	    enable_backlight();
536	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
537	
538	    /* Splash is up — let the app start everything else (services + camera) now,
539	     * in parallel with the screen painting below, so it's all warm at reveal. */
540	    if (s_splash_shown_cb != NULL) { s_splash_shown_cb(); }
541	
542	    /* Decode all album art into the RGB888 caches *before* building the screens,
543	     * so the song-select panel's initial selection (ScreenSongSelect_Setup ->
544	     * song_detail_show(0)) finds its cover already cached. Storage mounts here;
545	     * Legato's image decoders are up from SYS_Initialize. All behind the splash;
546	     * the ~1-3 s decode just extends the splash hold. See game/art.h. */
547	    (void)Art_LoadAll();
548	
549	    /* PHASE 2 — build the Marvin screen + per-panel setup behind the splash.
550	     * Scene-graph edits (screenInit_Marvin's leAddRootWidget calls) are guarded
551	     * against the render tasks; the canvas/layer binds after are GFX-canvas only
552	     * (no root-list mutation) so they need no guard. */
553	    scene_edit_begin();
554	    init_screens();
555	    scene_edit_end();
556	
557	    /* Dashboard live on BASE (covered by the splash until reveal). Nav and
558	     * song-select are built and painting into their own canvases but not bound to
559	     * a layer yet — they take their layers at reveal, once the splash vacates. */
560	    bind_canvas(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
561	
562	    /* Park HEO off (video hidden) so the dashboard owns the full panel until video
563	     * is shown at reveal. BASE discard is off by reset default and stays off until
564	     * the reconcile arms it. Was video.c's job at task start; the compositor owns HEO
565	     * now. Safe as a one-shot here — the video task's reconcile is a no-op while
566	     * video is hidden, so this is the only HEO writer at boot. */
567	    heo_unbind();
568	
569	    /* Paint all screens once now, behind the splash, then wait for it to drain.
570	     * Every surface is complete before it's ever shown; screens are event-driven
571	     * from here — showing one is a pure layer bind, no repaint. */
572	    paint_all_screens_once();
573	    wait_render_idle();
574	
575	    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
576	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
577	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
578	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
579	
580	    /* REVEAL — cut over to the (painted) dashboard. The song-select dialog starts
581	     * closed: it and its OVR2 cover strip are painted into their canvases but not
582	     * shown; UiManager_OpenSongSelect() binds + shows the pair on demand (header tap).
583	     * Set OVR1's colour mode to RGB565 now so the first nav-open (nav shares OVR1 and
584	     * doesn't poke RGBMODE itself) scans out correctly even before any dialog open. */
585	    ScreenSplash_Hide(xlcdc_layer(SPLASH_HW_LAYER));
586	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(xlcdc_layer(HW_OVR1), XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
587	
588	    /* Bring the live video up on HEO over the dashboard. Intent only — the video
589	     * task binds HEO on its next reconcile once the source is locked. */
590	    UiManager_VideoShow(VIDEO_WIN_X, VIDEO_WIN_Y, VIDEO_WIN_W, VIDEO_WIN_H);
591	
592	    /* Arm capture LAST — after the display is up and the boot-time task/SD/paint
593	     * contention has drained. The CSI-2 D-PHY RX is timing-sensitive at bring-up
594	     * (it must catch the source's LP11→HS transition); arming it earlier, during the
595	     * splash, makes it lock marginally and the lanes sit in stop-state (~0 fps). This
596	     * is the one ordering that must hold — see the journal (2026-06-30). */
597	    Video_CaptureEnable();
598	
599	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
600	}
601

620	     * the video task starts (Video_Initialize runs later, in APP_Tasks). The video
621	     * task then drives heo_reconcile each tick and the ISC IRQ drives heo_frame_latch. */
622	    Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(heo_frame_latch);
623	    Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(heo_reconcile);

625	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(ui_boot_task, "UiBoot", BOOT_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
626	                            NULL, BOOT_TASK_PRIORITY, s_boot_stack, &s_boot_tcb);
627	}

```text
1	# marvin — UI architecture (canvas compositor + per-screen modules)
2	
3	How marvin's operator UI is structured: independently-authored panels (dashboard, nav,
4	dialogs) each render into their own **canvas surface** in RAM, the compositor maps surfaces
5	onto the scarce **LCDC hardware layers**, and — with the MGS screen state machine disabled —
6	the application owns screen orchestration so multiple panels coexist **live and interactive
7	at once** instead of one-screen-at-a-time switching.
8	
9	Read [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.5 (operator UI) and §4.1 (video/display) first. Decisions in
10	[`journal.md`](journal.md) (2026-06-25, 2026-06-29). **Status: migrated to the MGS layer-screen
11	model and confirmed on hardware** — one master `Marvin` screen with dashboard (BASE), nav
12	(OVR1), and song-select dialog (OVR2) as layer-screens; the model and the canonical mental
13	picture are in §0.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 0. The mental model (read this first) — three concepts, not two
18	
19	These are distinct and must not be collapsed (this has been a recurring source of confusion):
20	
21	1. **Legato layer ("layer-screen")** — a logical screen / dialog / overlay. Bounded by
22	   `LE_LAYER_COUNT` = the number of layer-screens.
23	2. **GFX canvas** — the RAM framebuffer backing a layer-screen. **Coupled 1:1 to its Legato
24	   layer:** the renderer writes Legato layer *i* into `canvas[baseCanvasID + i]` (base 0 →
25	   layer *i* ↔ `canvas[i]`), and `leAddRootWidget(root, layerIdx)` rejects
26	   `layerIdx >= LE_LAYER_COUNT`. So a canvas id is **not** free of its Legato layer.
27	3. **XLCDC hardware layer** (`BASE`/`OVR1`/`OVR2`; `HEO` = camera) — where a canvas is
28	   composited for scanout. Bound at **display time, at runtime, and reassignable** via
29	   `gfxcSetLayer(canvasID, hwLayer)` (`ui_manager.c` `bind_canvas`).
30	
31	**"canvas ≠ layer" is true only for the *hardware* layer (3), not for the *Legato* layer (2).**
32	A panel never *owns* a HW layer — two canvases never shown together can share one; the same
33	canvas can be on `OVR1` in one situation and `OVR2` in another. The 8-slot canvas pool
34	(`CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ = 8`) means up to 8 layer-screens may be **defined**
35	(`LE_LAYER_COUNT` ≤ 8, canvases 0–7); the LCDC then composites **any 3** of them onto its 3
36	usable HW layers at once — *define many, show a few.*
37	
38	### 0.1 Direction (decided 2026-06-29): adopt MGS's single-master-screen / layer-screen model
39	
40	Per Microchip's GFX-canvas layer-screen guide¹, MGS is meant to be **one master screen whose
41	*layers* are the logical screens** ("layer-screens"), each auto-associated with its own canvas.
42	marvin **adopted this model on 2026-06-29** (confirmed on hardware). It previously *emulated*
43	it by hand — each panel a **separate 1-layer MGS Screen**, built on layer 0 then manually
44	disconnected and re-hosted by `ui_manager`, with `LE_LAYER_COUNT` pinned at 3 by a never-shown
45	`LayerBudget` screen. Now there is **one master screen named `Marvin`, one layer per panel**:
46	layer 0 dashboard (BASE), layer 1 nav (OVR1), layer 2 song-select dialog (OVR2). MGS derives
47	`LE_LAYER_COUNT` and associates each layer-screen with `canvas[i]`, so the `LayerBudget` hack
48	and the disconnect/re-host dance are gone — `ui_manager` calls `screenInit_Marvin()` +
49	`screenShow_Marvin()` once (the latter builds the tree and attaches each root to its Legato
50	layer), then per-panel `*_Setup()` wiring, and binds canvases to HW layers at display time.
51	**The splash is separate and fully manual** (pre-Legato RGBA8888 scanout): it is *not* a
52	canvas at all — it owns a static framebuffer and drives its XLCDC hardware layer directly via
53	the PLIB (`splash.c` `Splash_Show`/`Splash_Hide`, mirroring `video.c`'s HEO setup), so the
54	canvas pool is exactly the three layer-screens (0/1/2).
55	
56	> **§1–§7 below were written for the previous per-screen-Factory + manual-re-host design** and
57	> are kept for history; where they conflict with §0, §0 wins. `screenInit_X` is now a one-time
58	> flag only — the widget tree is constructed in **`screenShow_X`** (a gotcha worth remembering).
59	
60	¹ developerhelp.microchip.com → MGS Harmony guide → how-to → gfx-canvas → layer-screen.
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 1. The core idea
65	
66	Content geometry was welded to hardware 1:1:1 — one Legato layer → one framebuffer → one LCDC
67	layer. There are only **4 LCDC layers** (`BASE`, `OVR1`, `HEO`, `OVR2`); `HEO` is the live
68	camera. The compositor breaks the welding:
69	
70	- A **surface** is a RAM framebuffer (a GFX Canvas object) holding a panel's pixels.
71	- A **layer** is a hardware compositor window. The LCDC blends them every scan with zero CPU.
72	- Showing a panel = point a layer at its surface + enable (register writes, no re-render).
73	  Hiding = disable/move the layer. Sliding = animate the layer's window position.
74	
75	**GFX Canvas** is the substrate: `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer` redirects Legato's render target to a
76	canvas object, and `gfxcSetLayer`/`ShowCanvas`/`SetWindowPosition` map/show/move that surface
77	on an LCDC layer. (Why canvas and not a hand-rolled retarget or direct-layer-only: see the
78	2026-06-25 journal entry — canvas is the only thing that gets Legato content *into* an
79	arbitrary off-screen surface; direct layer control still does the show/move.)
80	
81	## 2. The enabling change — MGS screen state machine OFF
82	
83	Legato's stock "screen state machine" (`le_gen_init.c`) shows **one screen at a time** —
84	`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing screen's widget tree. That is fatal to a compositor
85	that wants several panels live simultaneously. So it is **disabled** ("Generate Screen State
86	Machine" off; `le_gen_init.{c,h}` no longer generated — see the 2026-06-25 journal entry and
87	the `compat/` stub that works around the resulting MGS include bug).
88	
89	Two confirmed facts make this work (verified in `legato_state.c` / `legato_renderer.c` /
90	`legato_input.c`):
91	
92	1. **`_state.layerList` is global and `leUpdate` renders/updates *every* attached layer each
93	   frame.** There is no "active screen" render gate. Attach roots to multiple layers → they all
94	   render live.
95	2. **Touch picks across all attached layers, top-to-bottom** (`leInput` iterates `layerList`
96	   from the top). So an attached overlay is interactive wherever it sits; the layer below
97	   receives touches elsewhere. *(This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable /
98	   reveal-then-promote" idea — that was a consequence of the state machine, which is now gone.)*
99	
100	So the model is simply: **attach a panel's root to a layer → it is live and interactive;
101	detach (or move off-screen) → it is gone.** No freeze, no promotion dance.
102	
103	## 3. MGS Screen = widget-tree factory
104	
105	With the state machine off, the generated per-screen functions are ours to call directly
106	(MGS even relabels them `// call to show this screen`). We treat each **MGS Screen as a
107	widget-tree factory**, decoupled from display:
108	
109	- `screenInit_X()` — builds the widget tree (+ registers any MGS-wired events).
110	- `screenShow_X()` — attaches its root(s) to layer(s) and raises the `X_OnShow` hook.
111	- `leAddRootWidget(wgt, layer)` / `leRemoveRootWidget(wgt, layer)` — **re-host** a root onto
112	  whatever Legato layer we want, independent of the index MGS authored it on.
113	- `screenGetRoot_X(lyrIdx)` — fetch a root to re-host or toggle visibility.
114	
115	So each panel is authored in its own clean MGS Screen, then the compositor assembles the
116	trees onto the layer set it manages. The screen's `OnShow` hook is that panel's
117	**composition root** — where it runtime-registers its widget event callbacks (the DI pattern;
118	see the 2026-06-25 journal entry on widget events being runtime-registerable while screen
119	lifecycle events are direct calls).
120	
121	## 4. Hardware layer budget
122	
123	| Legato layer | LCDC | Content | Lifecycle |
124	|---|---|---|---|
125	| 0 | BASE | active full-screen view (dashboard, …) | swappable (replace) |
126	| 1 | OVR1 | **nav drawer** | resident — attach once, persists across base-view swaps |
127	| 2 | OVR2 | **modal dialog** (song/mode select), sized to the dialog | shown/hidden; background stays live |
128	| — | HEO | camera | `video.c`, **outside Legato** |
129	
130	- **Nav on its own resident layer ⇒ "same nav over every view" for free** — it is independent
131	  of layer 0, so swapping the base view leaves it untouched.
132	- **Modal dialog on OVR2 sized to the dialog ⇒ uncovered dashboard telemetry keeps updating**
133	  (layer 0 renders live behind it). The dialog is invoked only from the dashboard.
134	- **Ceiling:** dashboard + nav + dialog + camera = **all 4 LCDC layers**. A 4th simultaneous UI
135	  surface needs canvas multiplexing (`gfxcSetBaseCanvasID`) or giving up a layer.
136	
137	### 4.1 Two layer counts — don't conflate them
138	- **`LE_LAYER_COUNT`** (Legato, `legato_config.h`) = how many canvases / Legato layers the global
139	  `layerList` manages = **3**. MGS derives it as the **max layer count across all screens** in the
140	  design; there is no explicit knob.
141	- **`XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS`** (XLCDC driver, "Total Layers" in `le_gfx_driver_xlcdc.yml`) = enumerated
142	  hardware layers = **4** (`layerOrder` = {BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2, OVR2 3}).
143	
144	They differ on purpose: Legato manages 3 canvases, each mapped onto **3 of the 4** hardware layers.
145	
146	### 4.2 Pinning `LE_LAYER_COUNT` = 3 (the LayerBudget screen)
147	Each panel is authored as its own **1-layer** MGS screen, so nothing reaches 3 layers on its own —
148	and there's no direct setting. A dedicated, **never-shown `LayerBudget` screen with 3 layers** pins
149	the count (regen-safe; no `legato_config.h` patch). Keep it un-shown: its roots then never attach,
150	so Legato layer 2 stays an empty internal root. **Caveat:** `LE_LAYER_COUNT` 3 lets Legato render
151	into `canvas[2]`, whose buffer is still the generated `NULL` until the dialog assigns one — safe
152	**only** while layer 2 has no attached root / no damage (i.e. LayerBudget is never shown and no panel
153	re-hosts onto layer 2 yet).
154	
155	### 4.3 Why HEO is safe (and stays enabled)
156	Layer targeting is **explicit, not positional**: Legato layer *i* → `canvas[i]` →
157	`gfxcSetLayer(i, hwLayer)`, where `hwLayer` indexes `layerOrder`. We map canvases only to hw layers
158	**0 / 2 / 3** (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) and **never to 1 (HEO)**, so the canvas framework never issues an
159	IOCTL to HEO regardless of enumeration order. The only GFX-side touch of HEO is
160	`DRV_XLCDC_Initialize` disabling all enumerated layers once at init — before `video.c` configures it
161	(post-scheduler), so video is the last writer. So **HEO stays enabled** and `video.c` keeps full
162	runtime control via the XLCDC PLIB, including the `HEOCFG12` blender + `VIDPRI` z-order that
163	`XLCDC_SetupHEOLayer` provides (`video.c` does not set those itself — which is exactly why disabling
164	HEO in MCC would break compositing, and why we don't).
165	
166	## 5. Live coexistence vs. replacement
167	
168	The compositor offers two verbs, chosen per interaction — you do **not** pick one global mode:
169	
170	- **Coexist (overlay-as-layer)** — the panel is its own layer over a still-live background.
171	  Used for the **nav drawer** (dashboard keeps updating behind it) and the **modal dialog**
172	  (telemetry keeps updating around it). No freeze.
173	- **Replace (switch base view)** — a full-screen view replaces another on layer 0; the
174	  outgoing one detaches (its surface can hold the last frame, or it is rebuilt on return).
175	  Used when a view genuinely supersedes the dashboard and live background isn't needed.
176	
177	Because the compositor owns layer placement and attach/detach, moving an interaction between
178	these is a compositor-level change, not a per-module rewrite — the reversibility we wanted.
179	
180	## 6. Module structure
181	
182	```
183	            ┌──────────────────────── ui_manager ─────────────────────────┐
184	            │ string-table init · screen init/show · root re-host onto     │
185	            │ layers · layer/canvas pool · visibility · verbs:             │
186	            │   show_view(X) · push_overlay(nav|dialog) · hide_overlay(…)   │
187	            └───────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────┘
188	              ┌─────▼─────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐
189	              │  dashboard │         │ screens/nav │          │ song_select  │
190	              │ (BASE,lyr0)│         │ (OVR1,lyr1) │          │ (OVR2,lyr2)  │
191	              └────────────┘         └─────────────┘          └──────────────┘
192	   each: owns its widgets + interactions; composition root = its screen OnShow hook
193	```
194	
195	- **`ui_manager`** (promoted from today's `compositor.c`) owns the *mechanism*: string-table
196	  setup, calling `screenInit_/screenShow_`, re-hosting roots onto the right layer, the canvas
197	  buffer pool, layer visibility, and the coexist/replace verbs. It is the "top-level module
198	  that ties everything together."
199	- **Per-screen/overlay modules** own only their panel's content + event wiring, registered
200	  from their own `OnShow` composition root. They never call `legato_*`/canvas APIs directly —
201	  they go through `ui_manager`, which is what keeps the layer mechanics swappable.
202	
203	### 6.1 Source layout (`default/src/ui/`)
204	
205	The UI tree is grouped by role; module files carry an explicit `screen_`/`widget_` prefix so
206	a flat editor tab list reads unambiguously:
207	
208	```
209	ui/
210	  ui_manager.{c,h}                          orchestrator (mechanism; stays at root)
211	  manual_input.c                            input shim for the future manual-input screen
212	  screens/<name>/   screen_<name>.{c,h}     one folder per panel (+ panel-specific helpers)
213	  widgets/<name>/   widget_<name>.{c,h}     reusable widgets, one folder each
214	```
215	
216	Current contents: `screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard`, `screens/navigation/screen_navigation`,
217	`screens/song_select/screen_song_select`, `screens/splash/screen_splash`,
218	`widgets/song_list/widget_song_list`, `widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa`.
219	
220	**Naming convention:** a screen module's file is `screens/<name>/screen_<name>.{c,h}` and its
221	public functions are prefixed `Screen<Name>_` (PascalCase of the file basename) — e.g.
222	`screen_song_select.c` → `ScreenSongSelect_Setup`. This matches the project's `Module_Method`
223	style (`UiManager_*`, `ButtonAA_*`) and stays clear of the MGS-generated entry points
224	(lowercase `screenInit_Marvin`, `event_Marvin_*`). Each panel module exposes
225	`Screen<Name>_InitSurface()` (assign its canvas buffer, pre-scheduler) and `Screen<Name>_Setup()`
226	(set its canvas window + wire content/events on the widgets `screenShow_Marvin` already built);
227	`ui_manager` calls these — the modules never bind HW layers themselves. The splash is the one
228	exception: it is not a canvas, so it exposes `ScreenSplash_Load`/`Show`/`Hide` instead. Headers
229	are included from the `default/src` root, e.g. `#include "ui/screens/navigation/screen_navigation.h"`.
230	New panels add a `screens/<name>/` folder; new widgets a `widgets/<name>/` folder — each wired
231	into `user.cmake`
232	(no MCC involvement).
233	
234	## 7. Build state & refactor plan
235	
236	**Built (committed):** GFX Canvas substrate; state machine off + app-owned `screenInit/Show`
237	(`compat/le_gen_init.h` stub); `ui_manager` orchestrator + dashboard on BASE; `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3

243	
244	**Next:**
245	1. **Author song/mode-select as its own MGS Screen;** assign `canvas[2]` a real buffer and have
246	   `ui_manager` host it on layer 2 (OVR2) as a modal (sized to the dialog, dashboard live behind).
247	   First real exercise of the coexist verb with a *live* background; the re-host + slide

251	
252	## 8. Static-allocation, cache & priority rules
253	
254	- **Static non-cached surfaces.** Each canvas surface is a file-scope static array in
255	  `.region_nocache` (no malloc), passed via `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`. They are CPU-rendered then
256	  read by the 2D engine / LCDC DMA, so non-cached is required (same policy as `FB_CACHE_NC`
257	  and the Legato scratch — 2026-06-24 cache-coherency fix). RGB565 to match the panel.
258	- **`GFX_CANVAS_Task`** is at UI-band priority 2 (set in the gfx_canvas yml), required even
259	  with FX off (drives `INIT→RUNNING`). It's a dynamic MCC task on heap_1 like the others.
260	- **Heap.** The canvas component pushed `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang via the
261	  malloc-failed hook; heap is now 65536 and the fault hooks emit a DBGU marker (2026-06-25).
262	
263	## 9. Memory budget
264	
265	`.region_nocache` is 32 MB, shared with the ISC capture pool (~10.5 MB) + Legato scratch
266	(0.5 MB). Full-screen RGB565 surface ≈ 2.0 MB; overlays sized to content are far less (nav
267	~320×800 ≈ 0.5 MB; a modal dialog smaller still). ~19 MB free after BASE + capture + scratch,
268	so **memory is not the binding constraint — the 3 UI layers are.**
269	
270	## 10. Open items
271	
272	- **Base-view replacement** — first exercised by the boot splash → dashboard handoff (§12).
273	  Still open: the *return* path (rebuild vs parked last-frame) and nav-persistence interaction
274	  when two interactive base views swap (the splash is non-interactive, so it didn't surface this).
275	- **Splash→dashboard transition** is a hard cut (the BASE buffer swaps from the 32bpp splash to
276	  the as-yet-unpainted RGB565 dashboard, so a frame of garbage/black is possible before the
277	  first dashboard paint). Acceptable for a one-time boot; smooth later by painting the dashboard
278	  into its buffer before re-binding the layer, or a brief fade.
279	- **Splash backlight timing** is a fixed settle (`SPLASH_RENDER_SETTLE_MS`) because the JPEG
280	  decode runs inside a Legato paint we can't cleanly join from the loader. Replace with a real
281	  paint-complete signal if the panel ever lights mid-decode.
282	- **Reveal-before-paint** — *resolved* by the pre-render/persistent model (§13): screens are now
283	  painted to completion off-screen before being revealed.
284	- **`manual_input.c` fate** — `Screen0` retired; the strum handlers now serve the Dashboard
285	  screen, so it stays until manual control is reworked.
286	- **Per-pixel alpha** — which (if any) overlay needs ARGB8888 over the camera vs. layer alpha.
287	
288	## 10a. Anti-aliased rounded button corners (done)
289	
290	The nav buttons use the widget `cornerRadius` (set in code — not exposed in MGS), but the
291	classic skin's rounded-rect fill draws corners with `leRenderer_ArcFill` (hard, stepped
292	edges). Smoothing is done **without touching Legato/MCC code** (`config/default/` is
293	off-limits), via a per-instance vtable re-point in `src/ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`:
294	
295	- `leWidget.fn` is a writable per-instance pointer to a `const` vtable. `ButtonAA_Enable`
296	  makes one shared writable copy of the button vtable, overrides only `_paint`, and points
297	  the button's `fn`/`widget.fn` at it. No `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` (not an MCC knob; unguarded
298	  `#define 0` in generated `legato_config.h`), no global RAM cost — scoped to re-pointed
299	  buttons.
300	- The wrapper runs the original paint (bg + label + border), then on `DONE` with the
301	  supported radius overdraws the four corners: sample the backdrop from each corner's
302	  extreme pixel (left untouched by the rounded fill), then blend a 1px transition band from
303	  a precomputed coverage mask via `leColorLerp` + `leRenderer_PutPixel`. Fill is read from
304	  the live scheme each paint, so highlight (selected/unselected) and pressed states track.
305	- Runs **in-pass** (damage → repaint → AA in one paint), so no timing/flicker window.
306	- Wired from `nav_buttons_init()`; currently nav-only. Extending app-wide is just calling
307	  `ButtonAA_Enable` from other screens' button init. Single radius (`BUTTON_AA_RADIUS`);
308	  other radii pass through unsmoothed.
309	
310	## 12. Boot splash (done — code-complete, pending hardware test)
311	
312	A full-screen photo splash is the first thing on the panel: the loader reads it off the SD card
313	into RAM, gets it onto BASE, and only then lights the backlight, so the panel never shows a
314	pre-splash/garbage frame. It's also the first real use of the **replace** verb (§5) and proves
315	the runtime-image path the album-art pre-load will reuse.
316	
317	- **Splash on its own OVR2 layer/canvas, drawn over the dashboard.** The `Splash` MGS screen
318	  (`le_gen_screen_Splash.c`: full-screen `Splash_Panel_0`, solid scheme fill) is kept as the base
319	  for the "every base view has an MGS component" convention; its only real content — the photo — is
320	  loaded, not authored, so `screens/splash/screen_splash.c` adds one `leImageWidget` onto
321	  `Splash_Panel_0` in code and points it at the in-memory JPEG (solid fill = fallback when there's
322	  no card/image). `ui_manager` re-hosts the splash onto **Legato layer 2 / canvas 2 / OVR2** (32bpp
323	  XRGB8888, full screen, topmost overlay) so it covers the BASE dashboard while the dashboard paints
324	  underneath; dropping OVR2 reveals the finished dashboard.
325	- **Runtime JPEG from SD.** The loader reads `/<card>/ui/splash.jpg` (≤1 MB, **baseline** JPEG —
326	  the decoder is baseline-only) into a static cache-aligned buffer; `Splash_SetImageJpeg` builds a
327	  runtime `leImage` (format `JPEG`, mode `RGB_888`, buffer = compressed bytes + length, mirroring a
328	  generated `leImage`) and sets it on the image widget. Legato's enabled JPEG decoder decodes on
329	  paint into the 32bpp canvas. The compressed buffer stays resident while the splash is shown.
330	- **OVR2 must be set to 32bpp by hand (driver gotcha).** The GFX-XLCDC driver
331	  (`drv_gfx_xlcdc.c`) assumes **every** layer is the project framebuffer format (`FB_COL_MODE` =
332	  RGB565, `FB_TYPE_SZ` = 2): its canvas commit path (`SET_LAYER_UNLOCK`) writes address/alpha/
333	  position/size/stride/enable but **never `RGBMODE`**, so a canvas's `GFX_IOCTL_SET_LAYER_COLOR_MODE`
334	  is captured in `drvLayer.pixelformat` and silently dropped. An RGBA8888 splash buffer therefore
335	  gets read by a still-RGB565 OVR2 → garbled. `ui_manager` fixes this with a direct
336	  `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR2, RGBA_8888, true)` after binding the splash canvas;
337	  the driver never rewrites RGBMODE, so it sticks (same runtime XLCDC poke `video.c` uses for HEO).
338	  BASE/OVR1 stay RGB565 = the default, so they need no poke. Full-screen ⇒ XSTRIDE gap is 0, so the
339	  driver's `FB_TYPE_SZ`-based stride calc is harmless here.
340	- **Backlight gating.** The backlight is a **GPIO** (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN` / PC18), *not* the LCDC
341	  PWM — `XLCDC_EnableBacklight()` only enables the LCDC's `LCD_PWM` dimming output, which isn't
342	  wired to this board's backlight (so calling it does nothing visible). `UiManager_EnableBacklight()`
343	  drives PC18 directly (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set()`, active-high assumed). The pin starts low at
344	  boot (MCC PIO config — the old "set high on start" that made the panel light too early is gone),
345	  so the panel stays dark until the loader calls this after the splash is painted. Video go-live
346	  (`Video_SetWindow`/`CaptureEnable`/`DisplayShow`) also moved into the loader, post-handoff, so the
347	  camera doesn't pop in over the splash.
348	- **Asset:** seed at `data/ui/splash.jpg` (1280×800), copied to the card's `/ui/splash.jpg`
349	  (mirrors the catalog `data/` convention).
350	
351	## 13. Pre-rendered, persistent per-screen canvases (done — code-complete, pending hardware test)
352	
353	Fixes the reveal-before-paint flash (§10): a screen used to be shown while Legato incrementally
354	painted its freshly-rebuilt tree, so unpainted regions flashed uninitialized-DRAM noise (~1–2 s for
355	the Dashboard's ~200-widget tree). The model is now the §1 ideal — **paint into an off-screen
356	surface, then reveal**:
357	
358	- **Every screen is persistent + owns a canvas.** MGS screens are set **persistent** (built once in
359	  `screenInit_*`, never torn down — `screenHide_*` no longer deletes), each re-hosted onto its own
360	  Legato layer → canvas → HW layer: Dashboard 0/0/BASE (RGB565), Nav 1/1/OVR1 (RGB565), Splash
361	  2/2/OVR2 (RGBA8888). `CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ` (8, expandable) gives room per screen; no
362	  `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` multiplexing needed.
363	- **Build pre-scheduler, then let the render task paint; the loader just waits.** All screens are
364	  built + hosted on their layers in `UiManager_Initialize` (pre-scheduler → no concurrency). Once
365	  the scheduler is up, the normal `LEGATO_Tasks` + `GFX_CANVAS_Task` pair paints them — a full-screen
366	  surface spans several scratch tiles (`LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1`, 512 KB ⇒ ~131 072 px @ 32bpp),
367	  and the scratch is freed by the canvas commit *between* render passes, which only happens when
368	  those tasks actually run. So the loader does **not** drive `leUpdate` or touch the scheduler — it
369	  yields and polls the public `leRenderer_IsIdle()`. Important: `leRenderer_IsIdle()` is just
370	  `frameState == LE_FRAME_READY`, which is **also true in the gaps between `leUpdate` calls** (which
371	  tick only every ~10 ms), so a single sample reads "done" mid-paint; `wait_render_idle` requires
372	  idle to hold **continuously for ≥120 ms** before trusting it. Boot sequence: load JPEG (retried —
373	  SDMMC isn't ready this early) → `Splash_SetImageJpeg` → `wait_render_idle`
374	  (splash + dashboard + nav all painted; idle = every layer's frame complete) →
375	  `UiManager_EnableBacklight` (first lit frame = complete splash, dashboard finished behind the OVR2
376	  splash) → *(asset pre-load — none yet)* → min on-screen hold → `UiManager_RevealDashboard`
377	  (hide OVR2 → finished dashboard) → video go-live → self-delete.
378	  - *Earlier mistake (corrected):* the loader first suspended `LEGATO_Tasks` and drove `leUpdate`
379	    itself. That fought the scheduler and was wrong twice over — one `leUpdate(0)` only fills one
380	    scratch tile (the rest bail on the locked scratch), and calling `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` in a tight
381	    loop doesn't free it (the commit completes between real task runs). Letting the normal tasks run
382	    and pending on idle is both correct and simpler.
383	  - **Scratch buffer sized for a full-screen tile.** With the stock 512 KB scratch a full-screen
384	    32bpp surface is ~8 tiles, and a JPEG re-decodes per tile (~8×) → slow. Bumped
385	    `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE_KB` 512 → **4096** (MGS Graphics setting) so `maxScratchPixels` ≈
386	    1.05 M ≥ 1280×800 → one tile = whole screen, one decode, one render pass. Cost: a single 4 MB
387	    nocache scratch (`LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 1`, widget buffer disabled) — fits the headroom; also
388	    makes the RGB565 dashboard one pass.
389	- **Open:** the splash stays attached to layer 2 after reveal (just hidden); the future modal dialog
390	  (also OVR2/layer 2) will need to detach it first.
391	
392	## 11. Relationship to spec §4.5 / Q5
393	
394	This answers spec **Q5** (Legato vs. custom UI) for the *presentation* layer: **Legato is the
395	renderer; a marvin `ui_manager` over GFX Canvas owns surface/layer composition and screen
396	orchestration.** Per-screen *authoring* stays in MGS (one Screen per panel); the compositor
397	assembles their trees onto hardware layers.
398

```text
leEventResult handleTouchDown(leWidgetEvent_TouchDown* evt)
{
    leWidget* targetWidget = NULL;
    int32_t x = 0;
    int32_t y = 0;
    int32_t i;
    leState* state = leGetState();
    leLayerState* layerState;

#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerRect layerRect;
#endif

    // find the topmost widget on the topmost layer for the touch event
    for(i = leGetState()->layerList.size - 1; i >= 0; i--)
    {
        layerState = (leLayerState*)leList_Get(&state->layerList, i);

        x = evt->x;
        y = evt->y;


// all layers look like they're at 0, 0 to legato
// however, the driver could be rendering them at different coordinates
// the event coordinates may need to be adjusted to account for this
#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
        layerRect.layer.id = i;
        layerRect.x = 0;
        layerRect.y = 0;
        layerRect.width = 0;
        layerRect.height = 0;

        leRenderer_DisplayInterface()->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_GET_LAYER_RECT, &layerRect);

        // need to remember this offset for subsequent touch down/move events
        _state.driverAdjustX = layerRect.x;
        _state.driverAdjustY = layerRect.y;

        x -= layerRect.x;
        y -= layerRect.y;
#endif

        targetWidget = leUtils_PickFromWidget(&layerState->root, x, y);

        if(targetWidget != NULL)
            break;
    }

    // no widget qualified
    if(targetWidget == NULL)
    {
        leSetFocusWidget(NULL);

        return LE_EVENT_HANDLED;
    }

    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_TRUE)
        return LE_EVENT_DEFERRED;

    evt->x = x;
    evt->y = y;

    while(targetWidget != NULL)
    {
        targetWidget->fn->_handleEvent(targetWidget, (leEvent*)evt);

        if(evt->event.accepted == LE_TRUE)
            break;

        targetWidget = targetWidget->parent;
    }

    if(evt->event.owner != NULL)
    {
        leSetFocusWidget(evt->event.owner);
    }
    // no widget claimed the event
    else
    {
        leSetFocusWidget(NULL);
    }

#ifdef INPUT_EVENT_DEBUG
    printf("handling touch down event %i, %i\n", evt->x, evt->y);
#endif

    return LE_EVENT_HANDLED;
}

leEventResult handleTouchUp(leWidgetEvent_TouchUp* evt)
{
    leWidget* wgt = leGetFocusWidget();

    if(wgt == NULL)
        return LE_EVENT_HANDLED;

    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_FALSE)
    {
#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
        evt->x -= _state.driverAdjustX;
        evt->y -= _state.driverAdjustY;
#endif

        wgt->fn->_handleEvent(wgt, (leEvent*)evt);

#ifdef INPUT_EVENT_DEBUG
        printf("handling touch up event %i, %i\n", evt->x, evt->y);
#endif

        return LE_EVENT_HANDLED;
    }

    return LE_EVENT_DEFERRED;
}

leEventResult handleTouchMoved(leWidgetEvent_TouchMove* evt)
{
    leWidget* wgt = leGetFocusWidget();

    if(wgt == NULL)
        return LE_EVENT_HANDLED;

    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_FALSE)
    {
#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
        evt->x -= _state.driverAdjustX;
        evt->y -= _state.driverAdjustY;
#endif
       wgt->fn->_handleEvent(wgt, (leEvent*)evt);

#ifdef INPUT_EVENT_DEBUG
```

```md
# Tap-to-fullscreen live video

## Context

On the marvin dashboard the live camera is shown in a 720×480 window (HEO layer)
at panel coords (280,76). The user wants to **tap the video to blow it up to
fullscreen, and tap again to shrink it back** to the dashboard window. There is
no dedicated home for this behaviour today, and the natural place is a
`screens/video/` module that owns the video-window interaction/state — mirroring
how every other panel gets its own `screen_<name>` module.

### Key facts established from the code
- **The video is on HEO, which Legato cannot pick.** HEO is owned by the
  compositor (`ui_manager.c`); the UI task only sets intent via
  `UiManager_VideoShow(x,y,w,h)` / `UiManager_VideoHide()`. The video-task
  reconcile rebinds HEO (with the bilinear/bicubic scaler when dst≠src), and
  `base_discard_reconcile` already makes BASE skip DMA behind the video rect — so
  a fullscreen rect gives a **full-screen BASE discard for free** (bandwidth win).
- **A tap on the video must be caught by a Legato widget.** `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`
  (layer 0, full-screen 1280×800, pickable) sits under `root0` (which is
  IGNOREPICK/IGNOREEVENTS). It is the full-screen catch-all.
- **Legato bubbles touch events up the parent chain** until one calls
  `leWidgetEvent_Accept` (`legato_input.c:401-408`). Plain panels (VIDEO_STREAM,
  BASE_*) never accept, so a tap on the video region bubbles up to
  `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`. Interactive widgets (header→song-select, buttons)
  *do* accept, so they don't bubble.
- **The dashboard's interactive widgets all live under exactly two panels:**
  `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP` (header) and `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM` (control
  columns + video + guitar). Clearing `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` on those two makes
  `leUtils_PickFromWidget` skip their whole subtrees, so **every** tap resolves to
  `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`. This is the same flag-only pick-gate idiom already
  used by `panel_set_pickable` in `ui_manager.c` (toggles pickability without
  invalidating/repainting).
- Fullscreen fit: **stretch to fill** (confirmed) = `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,1280,800)`.
  No letterbox math needed.

## Approach

Add a self-contained `screen_video` module that owns the fullscreen state, the two
rects, and the dashboard tap handler. It drives HEO purely through the existing
`UiManager_VideoShow` verb; `ui_manager` keeps owning the raw HEO mechanism.

### New: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.{c,h}`

Header exposes:
- `#define SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_X/Y/W/H` = `280/76/720/480` (the windowed rect —
  moved here from `ui_manager.c`'s `VIDEO_WIN_*`, now the single source of truth).
- `void ScreenVideo_Setup(void);` — wire the tap handler.
- `void ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed(void);` — force windowed state (used at reveal
  and on song-select close).

Implementation:
- `static bool s_fullscreen;`
- Re-point `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`'s vtable onto a shared writable copy whose
  `touchDownEvent` runs the toggle — the exact shared-vtable-copy pattern in
  `screen_dashboard.c:30-50` (`header_tap_opens`/`header_touchDown`).
- Handler `dashboard_touchDown(wgt, evt)`:
  - if `s_fullscreen` → `exit_fullscreen()` and `leWidgetEvent_Accept(&evt->event, wgt)`.
  - else if `evt->x/evt->y` inside the windowed rect → `enter_fullscreen()` + accept.
  - else → do nothing (leave unaccepted; normal dashboard behaviour is unaffected
    because interactive widgets accepted the event before it ever bubbled here).
- `enter_fullscreen()`: `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,BASE_W,BASE_H)`;
  gate off (`set_dashboard_input(false)`); `s_fullscreen = true`.
- `exit_fullscreen()` ≡ `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`: gate on;
  `UiManager_VideoShow(SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_*)`; `s_fullscreen = false`.
- `set_dashboard_input(on)`: static helper toggling `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` on
  `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP` and `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM` (flag-only, no repaint —
  same rationale as `ui_manager.c`'s `panel_set_pickable`).

### Modify `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c`
- Remove the `VIDEO_WIN_*` defines; `#include "ui/screens/video/screen_video.h"`.
- `init_screens()`: add `ScreenVideo_Setup();` (after `ScreenDashboard_Setup();`).
- Boot reveal (~line 590) and `UiManager_CloseSongSelect()` (~line 378): replace
  the two `UiManager_VideoShow(VIDEO_WIN_...)` calls with `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed();`
  (also resets fullscreen state cleanly whenever the dialog closes).
- `UiManager_VideoShow/Hide` and the whole HEO/discard/reconcile machinery: unchanged.

### Modify `firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`
- Add `.../default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.c` to the source list
  (alongside the other `screen_*.c` entries, ~line 16-20).

### Docs
- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`: new top entry — tap-to-fullscreen video +
  the `screen_video` module + the "gate BASE_TOP/BASE_BOTTOM → all taps bubble to
  PANEL_DASHBOARD" mechanism.
- `firmware/marvin/docs/ui_compositor.md` §6.1: add `screens/video/screen_video`

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Tap-to-fullscreen live video

## Context

On the marvin dashboard the live camera is shown in a 720×480 window (HEO layer)
at panel coords (280,76). The user wants to **tap the video to blow it up to
fullscreen, and tap again to shrink it back** to the dashboard window. There is
no dedicated home for this behaviour today, and the natural place is a
`screens/video/` module that owns the video-window interaction/state — mirroring
how every other panel gets its own `screen_<name>` module.

### Key facts established from the code
- **The video is on HEO, which Legato cannot pick.** HEO is owned by the
  compositor (`ui_manager.c`); the UI task only sets intent via
  `UiManager_VideoShow(x,y,w,h)` / `UiManager_VideoHide()`. The video-task
  reconcile rebinds HEO (with the bilinear/bicubic scaler when dst≠src), and
  `base_discard_reconcile` already makes BASE skip DMA behind the video rect — so
  a fullscreen rect gives a **full-screen BASE discard for free** (bandwidth win).
- **A tap on the video must be caught by a Legato widget.** `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`
  (layer 0, full-screen 1280×800, pickable) sits under `root0` (which is
  IGNOREPICK/IGNOREEVENTS). It is the full-screen catch-all.
- **Legato bubbles touch events up the parent chain** until one calls
  `leWidgetEvent_Accept` (`legato_input.c:401-408`). Plain panels (VIDEO_STREAM,
  BASE_*) never accept, so a tap on the video region bubbles up to
  `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`. Interactive widgets (header→song-select, buttons)
  *do* accept, so they don't bubble.
- **The dashboard's interactive widgets all live under exactly two panels:**
  `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP` (header) and `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM` (control
  columns + video + guitar). Clearing `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` on those two makes
  `leUtils_PickFromWidget` skip their whole subtrees, so **every** tap resolves to
  `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`. This is the same flag-only pick-gate idiom already
  used by `panel_set_pickable` in `ui_manager.c` (toggles pickability without
  invalidating/repainting).
- Fullscreen fit: **stretch to fill** (confirmed) = `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,1280,800)`.
  No letterbox math needed.

## Approach

Add a self-contained `screen_video` module that owns the fullscreen state, the two
rects, and the dashboard tap handler. It drives HEO purely through the existing
`UiManager_VideoShow` verb; `ui_manager` keeps owning the raw HEO mechanism.

### New: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.{c,h}`

Header exposes:
- `#define SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_X/Y/W/H` = `280/76/720/480` (the windowed rect —
  moved here from `ui_manager.c`'s `VIDEO_WIN_*`, now the single source of truth).
- `void ScreenVideo_Setup(void);` — wire the tap handler.
- `void ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed(void);` — force windowed state (used at reveal
  and on song-select close).

Implementation:
- `static bool s_fullscreen;`
- Re-point `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`'s vtable onto a shared writable copy whose
  `touchDownEvent` runs the toggle — the exact shared-vtable-copy pattern in
  `screen_dashboard.c:30-50` (`header_tap_opens`/`header_touchDown`).
- Handler `dashboard_touchDown(wgt, evt)`:
  - if `s_fullscreen` → `exit_fullscreen()` and `leWidgetEvent_Accept(&evt->event, wgt)`.
  - else if `evt->x/evt->y` inside the windowed rect → `enter_fullscreen()` + accept.
  - else → do nothing (leave unaccepted; normal dashboard behaviour is unaffected
    because interactive widgets accepted the event before it ever bubbled here).
- `enter_fullscreen()`: `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,BASE_W,BASE_H)`;
  gate off (`set_dashboard_input(false)`); `s_fullscreen = true`.
- `exit_fullscreen()` ≡ `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`: gate on;
  `UiManager_VideoShow(SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_*)`; `s_fullscreen = false`.
- `set_dashboard_input(on)`: static helper toggling `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED` on
  `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP` and `Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM` (flag-only, no repaint —
  same rationale as `ui_manager.c`'s `panel_set_pickable`).

### Modify `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c`
- Remove the `VIDEO_WIN_*` defines; `#include "ui/screens/video/screen_video.h"`.
- `init_screens()`: add `ScreenVideo_Setup();` (after `ScreenDashboard_Setup();`).
- Boot reveal (~line 590) and `UiManager_CloseSongSelect()` (~line 378): replace
  the two `UiManager_VideoShow(VIDEO_WIN_...)` calls with `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed();`
  (also resets fullscreen state cleanly whenever the dialog closes).
- `UiManager_VideoShow/Hide` and the whole HEO/discard/reconcile machinery: unchanged.

### Modify `firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`
- Add `.../default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.c` to the source list
  (alongside the other `screen_*.c` entries, ~line 16-20).

### Docs

  PANEL_DASHBOARD" mechanism.

## Notes / minor pre-existing quirks (not fixed here)

  which is what the user sees. Reconciling the two constants is out of scope.
- Entering fullscreen does not auto-close the nav drawer (OVR1) if it happens to be
  open; it would remain over the fullscreen video. Minor, deferred.

- Regressions to check: header tap still opens song-select (windowed); song-select
  open/close still restores the windowed video; robot-control / guitar buttons
  still respond when windowed.

```c
#include "ui/screens/video/screen_video.h"

#include "ui/ui_manager.h"   /* BASE_W, BASE_H, UiManager_VideoShow */

#include <stdbool.h>

#include "gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h"                     /* leWidget vtable + touch event */
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h"   /* dashboard panels */

/* Tap the live video to toggle fullscreen. The video is on HEO, which Legato
 * cannot pick, so the tap is caught on Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD — the full-screen
 * layer-0 panel every dashboard tap bubbles up to unless an interactive widget
 * accepts it first. Windowed: a tap inside the video rect enters fullscreen.
 * Fullscreen: BASE_TOP/BASE_BOTTOM picking is gated off (below) so every tap
 * resolves to the dashboard panel and exits. */

static bool s_fullscreen;

static leWidgetVTable s_dash_vt;
static void (*s_dash_touch)(leWidget *, leWidgetEvent_TouchDown *);
static leBool s_dash_vt_ready = LE_FALSE;

/* Gate the dashboard's interactive widgets from picking without repainting them.
 * All interactive widgets live under BASE_TOP (header) and BASE_BOTTOM (control
 * columns + video + guitar); leUtils_PickFromWidget descends only into ENABLED
 * children, so clearing the flag on those two makes every tap resolve to the
 * dashboard panel. Toggle the flag directly (not setEnabled) so the surface isn't
 * invalidated — same pick-only gate as ui_manager's panel_set_pickable. */
static void set_dashboard_input(bool on)
{
    if (on)
    {
        Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP->flags    |= LE_WIDGET_ENABLED;
        Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM->flags |= LE_WIDGET_ENABLED;
    }
    else
    {
        Marvin_PANEL_BASE_TOP->flags    &= ~LE_WIDGET_ENABLED;
        Marvin_PANEL_BASE_BOTTOM->flags &= ~LE_WIDGET_ENABLED;
    }
}

static void enter_fullscreen(void)
{
    UiManager_VideoShow(0u, 0u, BASE_W, BASE_H);
    set_dashboard_input(false);
    s_fullscreen = true;
}

void ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed(void)
{
    set_dashboard_input(true);
    UiManager_VideoShow(SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_X, SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_Y,
                        SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_W, SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_H);
    s_fullscreen = false;
}

static bool in_video_win(int32_t x, int32_t y)
{
    return x >= (int32_t)SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_X &&
           x <  (int32_t)(SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_X + SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_W) &&
           y >= (int32_t)SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_Y &&
           y <  (int32_t)(SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_Y + SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_H);
}

static void dashboard_touchDown(leWidget *wgt, leWidgetEvent_TouchDown *evt)
{
    if (s_dash_touch != NULL) { s_dash_touch(wgt, evt); }

    if (s_fullscreen)
    {
        ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed();
        leWidgetEvent_Accept(&evt->event, wgt);
    }
    else if (in_video_win(evt->x, evt->y))
    {
        enter_fullscreen();
        leWidgetEvent_Accept(&evt->event, wgt);
    }
}

void ScreenVideo_Setup(void)
{
    if (!s_dash_vt_ready)
    {
        s_dash_vt = *Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD->fn;
        s_dash_touch = Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD->fn->touchDownEvent;
        s_dash_vt.touchDownEvent = dashboard_touchDown;
        s_dash_vt_ready = LE_TRUE;
    }
    Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD->fn = &s_dash_vt;
}

```

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	**UI architecture — nav drawer complete; song/mode-select dialog is the next UI step.** The canvas compositor + per-screen-module model is built and validated on hardware: `ui_manager` orchestrates screens (string table + `screenInit/Show`; the MGS screen state machine is disabled, worked around with the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub), the dashboard is its own MGS Screen on BASE, and the nav drawer is its own MGS Screen (`Navigation`) re-hosted onto OVR1 — they coexist live (no active-screen gate; `leUpdate`/`leInput` cover all attached layers). `LE_LAYER_COUNT`=3 is pinned via the never-shown `LayerBudget` screen. **Nav drawer is feature-complete:** slides in/out via canvas Move FX (`NAV_CLOSED_X` dodges the window-clip row-wrap; mid-slide reversal cancels the in-flight move), single-active highlight (Dashboard closes, others switch), clean close, rounded buttons with anti-aliased corners (`ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c`, per-instance vtable re-point — see `ui_compositor.md` §10a). Authoritative design + the window-clip/alignment gotchas in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md); decisions 2026-06-25. **Next (decided 2026-06-29): migrate to MGS's single-master-screen / layer-screen model** — one master Legato screen named `Marvin` with one layer per panel (dashboard, nav, song-select, dialogs…), replacing the current "separate 1-layer MGS Screen per panel, manually re-hosted, `LE_LAYER_COUNT` pinned by the fake `LayerBudget` screen" approach. MGS then derives `LE_LAYER_COUNT` and auto-associates each layer-screen with its canvas, so the `LayerBudget` hack, the `compat/le_gen_init.h` stub, and the disconnect/re-host dance all go away; `ui_manager` shrinks to buffer assignment + `show_layer`/`hide_layer` verbs. **Splash stays separate/manual** (pre-Legato RGBA8888) on a canvas slot outside the layer-screen range. Authoritative model + direction now in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §0. SongSelect (MGS screen already generated, committed `1e16ac9`) becomes a Marvin layer-screen rather than a standalone Screen. The earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" framing is **superseded** (a state-machine artifact).
8	
9	**Song-select operator UI — scrollable list widget built & validated on hardware.** Custom Legato widget `ui/song_list.{h,c}` (a hand-written `leWidget` subclass) renders the SELECT SONG setlist (tier badge + bold title + dim artist + right-aligned duration), driven by a decoupled row-provider callback (no catalog dependency); drag-scroll with time-based kinetic inertia, tap-to-select. Bring-up via the `songlist` console command + a catalog-backed demo provider (`ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}`) — scroll/select/opaque-fill confirmed on hardware. **Bringing it up surfaced and fixed a real Legato/GFX2D cache-coherency bug** (see decision log 2026-06-24): the CPU-rendered scratch buffer was cacheable, so the 2D-engine blit leaked stale pixels through opaque widgets — fixed by placing the scratch in non-cached DDR. **Next:** author the full SELECT SONG screen in MGS (album art + catalog-fed metadata panel + difficulty/mode/Select), and the **tier / career-setlist data model** (the `tier` badge needs the deferred catalog tier column). Two upstream Microchip Legato/gfx bugs to file (decision log).

## Summary

Added tap-to-fullscreen live video via a new self-contained `screen_video` module, matching your instinct that the video-window logic deserves its own `ui/screens` home.

**New files**
- [screen_video.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.h) — `SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_*` (the windowed rect, now the single source of truth) + `ScreenVideo_Setup()` / `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`.
- [screen_video.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.c) — owns the fullscreen state and the tap interaction. It re-points `Marvin_PANEL_DASHBOARD`'s `touchDownEvent` (the shared-vtable-copy idiom from `screen_dashboard.c`).

**How it works** — the video is on HEO, which Legato can't pick, so the tap is caught on the full-screen dashboard panel that touches bubble up to:
- **Windowed → fullscreen:** a tap inside the video rect → `UiManager_VideoShow(0,0,1280,800)` (HEO scaler stretches to fill). `base_discard_reconcile` follows the rect, so BASE DMA is discarded across the whole panel — a free bandwidth win.
- **Fullscreen → exit:** picking is gated off on `BASE_TOP` + `BASE_BOTTOM` (the two subtrees holding every interactive widget) by clearing `LE_WIDGET_ENABLED`, so **any** tap resolves to the dashboard panel and returns to the windowed rect.

**Wiring** — [ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c): include + `ScreenVideo_Setup()` in `init_screens`, and `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()` at reveal and on song-select close (replacing the old inline `UiManager_VideoShow(VIDEO_WIN_*)`). Added the source to [user.cmake](firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake:17).

**Docs** — journal top entry + `ui_compositor.md` §14 and §6.1 list.

Two things to note:
- I couldn't compile here (no ARM/xc32 toolchain in the sandbox) — needs an MPLAB build + hardware test as the plan's verification section describes.
- Deferred quirks flagged in the plan: the windowed HEO rect (280,76) is offset from the `VIDEO_STREAM` placeholder panel (268,12), and entering fullscreen won't auto-close an open nav drawer.

Want me to reconcile that HEO/placeholder offset while we're here, or leave it?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 15:52:49Z)**_

Here's exactly what's happening, from the HEO scaler config in [ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c#L161-L183) (the fullscreen path just feeds a bigger `dst` into the same `heo_bind`):

## What we use now

When `dst != src` (i.e. fullscreen, and any non-1:1 window), `heo_bind` enables the HEO polyphase scaler and selects the **predefined bicubic (4-tap)** kernel for *both* axes and *both* planes:

```c
HEOCFG23 = V/H luma+chroma scaler enable
HEOCFG30 = VXSYCFG(1)|VXSYBICU(1) | VXSCCFG(1)|VXSCBICU(1)   // vertical bicubic
HEOCFG31 = HXSYCFG(1)|HXSYBICU(1) | HXSCCFG(1)|HXSCBICU(1)   // horizontal bicubic
HEOCFG24..27 = 12.20 fixed-point scale factors (src/dst)
```

The `*BICU_1` bit selects the hardware's built-in bicubic coefficient set, so we don't program any coefficient tables. This mirrors MCC's surface-set path. For our ~480p source → 1280×800 that's roughly a 1.78×/1.67× **upscale with bicubic**.

## What the fixed-function scaler actually offers

The HEO scaler is a fixed 4-tap-max polyphase FIR. Per the DFP register defs, the only real knobs are:

| Option | Bits | Character |
|---|---|---|
| **Bicubic, 4-tap** (current) | `*BICU=1` | Sharpest HW option; best for upscale; can ring/halo slightly on hard edges (text, gem borders) |
| **Bilinear, 2-tap** | `*TAP2=1` | Softer, cheaper (2 fetches vs 4); no ringing but blurrier |
| Tap centering | `*1201N` | left- vs center-aligned 2-tap phase |
| Scaler off | `*EN=0` | nearest/no interp (used automatically at 1:1) |

There is **no** higher-order option (no Lanczos, no edge-directed, no custom coefficient table exposed). So **bicubic is the highest-quality mode the silicon has**, and it's the correct default for upscaling game video — we're already using the best available kernel.

## The real quality limiters (not the kernel)

For Guitar Hero video the interpolation choice is secondary to two things:

1. **Aspect distortion** — 3:2 source stretched to 8:5 panel = ~7% horizontal over-stretch, so note gems/circles go slightly egg-shaped. This is the stretch-to-fill choice you made; letterboxing (declined) is the only fix, and it's a rect change, not a scaler change.
2. **Non-integer upscale** inherently softens vs native — unavoidable at this panel size.

If bicubic ringing on the note-highway edges ever looks objectionable in motion, the one lever worth trying is switching to **bilinear** for a softer look — but I'd expect bicubic to look better for this content. Both are a one-line register change if you want to A/B it on hardware.

One doc nit I noticed while checking: the comment above `heo_bind` (~line 131) says "engaging the bilinear scaler," but the code selects bicubic — stale wording worth fixing. Want me to correct that comment (and optionally add a compile-time switch to A/B bilinear vs bicubic)?

    sizes.add(im.shape); imgs.append(im)
print("shapes:", sizes)

stack = np.stack(imgs)                 # (N,H,W,3)
N, H, W = stack.shape[0], stack.shape[1], stack.shape[2]
lum_max = stack.max(axis=(0,3))        # per-pixel max across corpus+channels -> (H,W)

print("\n== corpus-wide content bounding box vs threshold ==")
for thr in (0,4,8,12,16,24,32):
    mask = lum_max > thr
    rows = np.where(mask.any(axis=1))[0]; cols = np.where(mask.any(axis=0))[0]
    if len(rows)==0 or len(cols)==0:
        print(f"thr>{thr:2d}: empty"); continue
    top,bot,left,right = rows[0],rows[-1],cols[0],cols[-1]
    print(f"thr>{thr:2d}: x[{left}..{right}] y[{top}..{bot}] w={right-left+1} h={bot-top+1}"
          f"  borders L{left} R{W-1-right} T{top} B{H-1-bot}")

# Edge vs interior black: are border pixels exactly 0 while in-video black > 0?
print("\n== value stats ==")
edge = np.concatenate([stack[:,0:2,:,:].ravel(), stack[:,-2:,:,:].ravel(),
                       stack[:,:,0:2,:].ravel(), stack[:,:,-2:,:].ravel()])

inner = stack[:,40:440,60:660,:]
print(f"interior(60:660,40:440): min={inner.min()} %<=4 {100*(inner<=4).mean():.3f} %==0 {100*(inner==0).mean():.4f}")

# Per-edge profile: how far in until content appears (max luma per row/col over corpus)
row_prof = lum_max.max(axis=1); col_prof = lum_max.max(axis=0)
def first_gt(prof, thr):
    idx = np.where(prof>thr)[0]; return (idx[0], idx[-1]) if len(idx) else (None,None)
for thr in (0,8,16):
    t,b = first_gt(row_prof,thr); l,r = first_gt(col_prof,thr)
    print(f"thr>{thr:2d}: top={t} bot={b} left={l} right={r}")

print("\n== first/last 12 col-profile & row-profile values (thr scan) ==")
print("cols[0:12] :", col_prof[:12].tolist())
print("cols[-12:] :", col_prof[-12:].tolist())
print("rows[0:12] :", row_prof[:12].tolist())
print("rows[-12:] :", row_prof[-12:].tolist())

import numpy as np, glob
from PIL import Image
files = sorted(glob.glob("*.png"))

def detect(lum, pedestal=None, margin=24, ss=2):
    # lum: (H,W) channel-max. Estimate pedestal from extreme edge rows (row0,rowH-1).
    H,W = lum.shape
    if pedestal is None:
        pedestal = int(np.median(np.concatenate([lum[0],lum[-1],lum[:,0]*0+lum[0].min()])))
    thr = pedestal + margin
    rmax = lum.max(axis=1); cmax = lum.max(axis=0)
    rows = np.where(rmax>thr)[0]; cols = np.where(cmax>thr)[0]
    if len(rows)==0 or len(cols)==0: return None
    return rows[0], rows[-1], cols[0], cols[-1], pedestal

bad=[]; ok=0

Analysis done — and it **overturns the hypothesis**, in a useful way. Single-frame detection recovered the exact active box on **101/101** captures.

## What the corpus shows

**Active video area = x[0…715], y[15…462] → 716×448 at offset (0,15).**
Dead bars: **top 15 px, bottom 17 px, right ~4 px, left 0 px.**

The transitions are razor-sharp and rock-solid across all 101 diverse screens (every screen is dark in rows 0–14 and 463–479):

| edge | last border row/col | first content row/col | jump (max luma) |
|---|---|---|---|
| top | row 14 (max 13) | row 15 (max 216) | 13 → 216 |
| bottom | row 463 (max 13) | row 462 (max 205) | 13 → 205 |
| right | col 716 (max 31) | col 715 (max 145) | ~13 → 145 |
| left | — | col 0 (max 190) | content at the edge |

## Your hypothesis was inverted — and that matters

The borders are **not 0**. They sit at a **black pedestal ≈ 13 max / ≈ 5.7 mean** (limited-range black from the component→HDMI A/D). Pure-zero pixels barely exist (1,532 in the entire corpus). And in-video black sits at the *same* pedestal (histogram peaks at value 5–7). So a `>0` test can't separate border from content — they overlap.

**What separates them cleanly is flatness/brightness, not zero:** border strips stay flat at the pedestal (per-row max ~13, cross-frame std ~0.9) while active content spikes to 150–216 (std ~50). So the rule is `value > pedestal + margin`, with the pedestal *measured*, not assumed.

## Proposed sampling routine (validated on the corpus)

```
detect_active_rect(frame):                 # RGB888, subsample ~every 2–4 px
  luma(px)   = max(R,G,B)                   # cheap; worked on all 101
  pedestal   = median(luma of row 0 + row H-1)   # extreme rows are always black bar
  thr        = pedestal + MARGIN (~24)
  row_max[y] = max luma over x;  col_max[x] = max luma over y
  top    = first y from 0    with row_max[y] > thr
  bottom = first y from H-1  with row_max[y] > thr
  left   = first x from 0    with col_max[x] > thr
  right  = first x from W-1  with col_max[x] > thr
  return rect, guarded (plausible size / spans enough) else None
```

Guards for the **dark-screen catch** you flagged (the corpus has no *fully* black frame — dimmest p99 was still 144 — but real loading/transition frames will be):
- Skip frames whose overall brightness is below a floor (can't detect on near-black).
- The bars are **fixed converter geometry**, so: detect on the first few *qualified* (bright) frames after source-lock, take the consensus/median, **cache it**, and hold last-good across dark frames. A per-pixel max-hold over ~K frames is the belt-and-suspenders version.

## The payoff (bigger than I expected)

Feed the detected rect as the **HEO source rectangle** — offset the layer base by `top*stride (+left*bpp)`, set `HEOCFG4` XMEMSIZE/YMEMSIZE to 716×448, and the line-stride gap to skip cropped columns (`heo_frame_latch` adds the same offset per ring slot). Then the scaler crops the console's dead bars and fills the window/fullscreen with *only* live video.

And the aspect bonus: **716×448 = 1.598, vs the panel's 1280×800 = 1.600** — essentially identical. So cropping to the active area makes **fullscreen almost perfectly aspect-correct**, which erases most of the ~7% stretch I flagged earlier.

**Fit:** detection + the active rect belong in `video.c` (it owns the frame/format/ring); the compositor's `heo_bind` consumes the rect as the source crop; `screen_video` still owns windowed/fullscreen dst. Orthogonal — it improves both modes.

Want me to turn this into an implementation plan (video.c detector + HEO source-crop wiring), or keep iterating on the routine first? I haven't written any code or touched the journal yet.
