```text
=== video.h ===
#ifndef VIDEO_H
#define VIDEO_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "queue.h"

/* Video pipeline: HDMI source → TC358743 bridge → CSI-2 → CSI2DC → ISC →
 * DDR. This module is the capture *producer*: it owns its own FreeRTOS task
 * (tc358743, isc_capture, capture state machine) and fans completed frames out
 * to subscribers from the ISC IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR.
 *
 * Display (the HEO hardware layer that scans a captured frame to the LCD) is
 * owned by the compositor (ui_manager), NOT here — capture and display are fully
 * independent (the detector/gameplay consume frames whether or not HEO is shown).
 * The module notifies the compositor through two registered callbacks so the
 * compositor can own all HEO/BASE register writes while keeping the timing this
 * task/IRQ already has:
 *   - a display-reconcile callback, called each task tick with the current source
 *     validity + size, so the compositor can (re)bind/unbind HEO in task context;
 *   - a frame-latch callback, called from the ISC IRQ with the freshest completed
 *     buffer address, so the compositor can latch HEO to the newest ring slot.
 *
 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, no callbacks. */

void Video_Initialize(void);

/* Capture chain control. ENABLE: arm ISC + bridge stream when source
 * is locked, re-arm on every lost/regain cycle. DISABLE: stop ISC +
 * stream and stay off regardless of lock state. */
void Video_CaptureEnable(void);
void Video_CaptureDisable(void);

/* Register the compositor's HEO hooks (see the module note above). Both are
 * optional (NULL = no display). Set before the video task starts.
 *   frame-latch: fires in ISC IRQ context with the just-completed buffer address.
 *   reconcile:   fires each task tick with (source_valid, src_w, src_h). */
void Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(void (*cb)(uint32_t buffer_addr));
void Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(void (*cb)(bool source_valid,
                                                  uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h));

/* Frame metadata delivered to subscribers on every captured frame. */
typedef struct
{
    void    *buffer;          /* pointer to most-recent complete frame in DDR */
    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
    uint16_t width;
    uint16_t height;
    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
} Video_FrameInfo;

/* Subscribe a queue to frame-ready events. The video module sends a
 * Video_FrameInfo from the ISC frame-done IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR
 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed
 * queue. Create the queue with:
 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
 *
 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
 * independently.
 *
 * The Video_FrameInfo.buffer pointer reflects the buffer that *just*
 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
 * second-next frame.
 *
 * Returns false if the subscriber table is full. Calling with a queue
 * already in the table is a no-op success. Up to VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS
 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */
bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);

/* Remove a queue from the subscriber list. Returns false if not found. */
bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);

/* Synchronous read of the current frame state. Doesn't block. May
 * report frame_count = 0 / buffer = NULL if capture has never armed. */
void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info);

#endif
```

```text
161	 * the capture chain, which re-inits the D-PHY and re-locks cleanly once the bus
162	 * is quiet. The frame-count reference is reset after each re-arm (ISC_Capture_-
163	 * Configure zeroes the counter), so a stuck source retries at most once per
164	 * window rather than every tick. */
165	static void capture_watchdog(void)
166	{
167	    static uint32_t  last_count;
168	    static TickType_t last_advance_tick;
169	
170	    /* Not actively capturing: hold the reference fresh so a subsequent arm gets
171	     * a full timeout window before it can look stalled. */
172	    if (!s_capture_armed || !s_capture_enabled || !TC358743_IsLocked())
173	    {
174	        last_count        = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
175	        last_advance_tick = xTaskGetTickCount();
176	        return;
177	    }
178	
179	    uint32_t  count = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
180	    TickType_t now  = xTaskGetTickCount();
181	
182	    if (count != last_count)
183	    {
184	        last_count        = count;
185	        last_advance_tick = now;
186	        return;
187	    }
188	
189	    if ((now - last_advance_tick) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS))
190	    {
191	        LOG_WARN("VIDEO: capture stalled at frame %lu (source locked) — re-arming\r\n",
192	                 (unsigned long)count);
193	        /* Dump the pipeline register state for the first few collapses so the
194	         * error class is visible without flooding the UART on every re-arm. */
195	        static uint8_t diag_budget = 8u;
196	        if (diag_budget > 0u) { ISC_Capture_DumpDiag("stall"); diag_budget--; }
197	        capture_disarm();
198	        s_capture_armed = false;
199	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
200	
201	        last_count        = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
202	        last_advance_tick = xTaskGetTickCount();
203	    }
204	}
```

```python
import numpy as np, glob
from PIL import Image
files = sorted(glob.glob("*.png"))

def detect(lum, thr, colstep=8, rowstep=8, minw=700, minh=420):
    H,W = lum.shape
    rmax = lum[:, ::colstep].max(axis=1)
    cmax = lum[::rowstep, :].max(axis=0)
    r = np.where(rmax>thr)[0]; c = np.where(cmax>thr)[0]
    if len(r)==0 or len(c)==0: return None
    top,bot,left,right = r[0],r[-1],c[0],c[-1]
    w,h = right-left+1, bot-top+1
    if w<minw or h<minh: return ("REJECT", top,bot,left,right,w,h)
    return ("OK", top,bot,left,right,w,h)

for thr in (40,48,64):
    boxes={}; rej=0; none=0
    for f in files:
        lum=np.asarray(Image.open(f).convert("RGB")).max(axis=2)
        r=detect(lum,thr)
        if r is None: none+=1; continue
        if r[0]=="REJECT": rej+=1; continue
        key=r[1:]; boxes[key]=boxes.get(key,0)+1
    print(f"\nthr={thr}: none={none} rejected={rej} accepted={sum(boxes.values())}")
    for k,v in sorted(boxes.items(), key=lambda x:-x[1])[:6]:
        top,bot,left,right,w,h=k
        print(f"  x[{left}..{right}] y[{top}..{bot}] {w}x{h}  ({v} frames)")

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 16:26:22Z)**_

Done. Here's what I built.

## Offline finding (from the 101-frame corpus)
Active area ≈ **716×448 @ (0,15)** — top 15 / bottom 17 / right 4 / left 0 px of dead bars. Your hypothesis was **inverted**: the bars aren't `0`, they sit at a ~13 pedestal — the *same* level as in-video black, so a `>0` test can't separate them. What does separate cleanly: **brightness** (border ≤14, content ≥145). A fixed luma threshold of 40 recovered the exact box on 99/101 frames, all 101 passing your ≥700×420 gate. Bonus: 716×448 = 1.598 ≈ the panel's 1.600, so cropping makes fullscreen essentially aspect-correct.

## Implementation

**`video.c` / `video.h` — runtime detector** (`Video_GetActiveRect`):
- Runtime, as you asked (varies per Wii/converter). `max(B,G,R) > 40` — no pedestal assumption.
- Scans inward from each edge, **bounded to the deepest border your min-size gate allows**, so a dark loading frame stays cheap (~1 ms, not ~17 ms).
- **Unions bright-pixel bounds over 16 *bright* frames** then locks — dark frames find no content and are skipped, so a loading screen at capture start just defers the lock (handles the "almost full black" catch you flagged). Rejects and retries if the union is < 700×420.
- **One-shot per capture arm**, reset on re-arm/source-size change; **full-frame fallback** until locked, so display always works.

**`ui_manager.c` — HEO source-crop** in `heo_bind`: offsets the frame base by `y*stride + x*bpp`, sizes `HEOCFG4` to the active rect, and skips cropped columns via `XSTRIDE=(src_w-aw)*bpp` (verified against the GFX driver's own `FB_TYPE_SZ*(resx-sizex)`). `heo_frame_latch` adds the crop offset per ring slot; `heo_reconcile` rebinds when detection flips full→cropped. Bars are cropped in both windowed and fullscreen.

Docs updated (journal + `ui_compositor.md` §15). **Code-complete, pending hardware test** — I can't compile here (no cross-toolchain in the sandbox).

One thing worth your eye on hardware: the detector logs `VIDEO: active area WxH @(x,y)` on lock — confirm it reports ~716×448 @ (0,15) on your actual Wii. Want me to leave it there, or also add a small CLI command to print the current active rect on demand? And I haven't committed — say the word.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 16:38:32Z)**_

Confirmed the formats: `ARGB_4444`, `ARGB_1555`, `ARGB_8888`, `RGBA_8888`, etc. Here's the assessment.

## Feasibility: yes, and the z-order is on our side
`VIDPRI(0)` → **OVR2 > OVR1 > HEO > BASE**. The two overlays sit *above* the video, so an overlay layer can paint on top of the video's edges. That's exactly what's needed — and it's why this works at all.

## Why the existing AA trick doesn't transfer
`PanelAA`/`ButtonAA` (compositor §10a) get their AA by **sampling the backdrop from the same canvas** and blending. Here the backdrop is HEO (the live video), which isn't in any canvas — Legato can't read it. So we can't blend against it in software. The fix is to stop trying to blend in software and instead lay down **true per-pixel alpha** and let the LCDC hardware composite the overlay over HEO. That's the whole reason an ARGB overlay is the right tool.

## Your core question — RGBA5551/ARGB1555 for AA: no
1-bit alpha is **on/off only** — zero intermediate coverage, so rounded corners come out hard-and-jagged. It cannot anti-alias. The gradation you need lives entirely in the alpha channel:

| Format | Alpha levels | AA result | Overlay cost @720×480·60fps |
|---|---|---|---|
| ARGB_1555 (≈"RGBA5551") | 2 | **jagged, unusable** | 41 MB/s |
| **ARGB_4444** | 16 | **good** — smooth across a 1–2 px band | ~41 MB/s |
| ARGB_8888 / RGBA_8888 | 256 | best | ~83 MB/s |

For a thin border at radius ~4 px, **ARGB_4444's 16 alpha steps look smooth** and cost half the bandwidth of 8888. Color depth (4 bits/channel) is irrelevant for a single-color frame — only the alpha ramp matters. So: ARGB_4444 is the sweet spot; ARGB_8888 if you want headroom; ARGB_1555 is out.

## Proposed approach
A **static hand-drawn ARGB overlay**, driven splash-style (not a Legato canvas):
- Sized to the fixed windowed video rect (720×480). Mostly transparent (alpha 0 → video shows through); only the rounded border ring + AA corners are painted. Precompute the coverage/alpha **once** at init — exact analytic AA, cleaner than Legato's hard `ArcFill`.
- Bind it to **OVR2** (above HEO) only for the windowed dashboard. Using OVR2 (not OVR1) lets it **coexist with the nav drawer** (OVR1); it's dropped when song-select opens (video is hidden then anyway) and not shown in fullscreen (edge-to-edge, no frame). Precedent: the splash already shares a HW layer with a canvas at different times.
- The windowed dst rect is fixed regardless of the active-crop work (crop changes the *source*, not the dst), so the overlay geometry is static — draw once, bind/unbind only.

## The one real caveat
It's an **always-on full-rect DDR read** whenever windowed video shows (~41 MB/s at ARGB_4444) on top of BASE+HEO. Given how CSI-2 D-PHY lock is sensitive to GFX bursts (per the journal), ARGB_4444 is the safer pick, and the existing BASE discard already frees the region behind the video so the net add is just this overlay. Worth watching for capture stalls on hardware — if it aggravates them, that's the knob.

Want me to plan/build it (static ARGB_4444 corner-frame overlay on OVR2, wired into `screen_video`'s windowed/fullscreen transitions)? I haven't touched anything — this is just the design.

```text
118	static void navigation_slide_to(int target_x)

132	     * closed). gfxcSetLayer needs the canvas hidden — it is, until gfxcShowCanvas
133	     * below. Caller ensures the dialog isn't holding OVR1. */
134	    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_NAVIGATION, HW_OVR1);
135	    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_NAVIGATION);

137	    /* Modal: gate the dashboard beneath so nothing behind the drawer reacts. The
138	     * drawer (on OVR1) covers the hamburger, so close is via the drawer's Dashboard
139	     * entry, not the hamburger — gating the dashboard loses no affordance. */
140	    UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(false);

147	     * disables the layer. NAVIGATION_CLOSED_X avoids the -NAVIGATION_W window-clip
148	     * row-wrap (see its definition); the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch,
149	     * so the final frame is displayed before the hide lands — keeping it in-bounds
150	     * makes that frame a harmless edge sliver instead of the panel's left columns. */
151	    navigation_slide_to(NAVIGATION_CLOSED_X);

163	 * mid-close restarts the move (so this won't fire for the abandoned close).
164	 * Re-arming dashboard input happens here too, only after OVR1 is freed, so no
165	 * mid-slide tap can open a modal onto the layer this hide is about to disable. */
166	static void navigation_fx_done(unsigned int canvasID, GFXC_FX_TYPE effect,
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 16:47:51Z)**_

Two decisive facts before I plan:

1. **The canvas framework can't do ARGB_4444** — its `gfxColorMode` enum only has `RGBA_5551`, `RGBA_8888`, `ARGB_8888` as alpha modes (no 4444). But the XLCDC *hardware* scanout does support `ARGB_4444`. So to get your 4444, the overlay must be a **direct-driven layer** (own framebuffer + XLCDC PLIB), like the splash and HEO — not a GFX canvas. That's fine and actually consistent with how video/splash already work.
2. `LE_LAYER_COUNT=4`, `CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ=8` — plenty of headroom, but since we're going direct-driven the border doesn't consume a canvas slot anyway.

Let me write the plan.

```md
# Rounded AA border/frame around the windowed video

## Context

The windowed live video on the dashboard is a hard-edged rectangle on the HEO
hardware layer. We want a **1px rounded frame** (radius 6, color `0x404040` to
match the dashboard panels' `LE_SCHM_SHADOWDARK` border) with **anti-aliased
rounded corners**. Because the video is on HEO (not a Legato canvas), the
`PanelAA`/`ButtonAA` backdrop-sampling trick can't reach it — the corners must be
cut/framed by an overlay *above* HEO that carries **true per-pixel alpha**, letting
the LCDC composite it over the video.

Key facts established:
- **Z-order is `OVR2 > OVR1 > HEO > BASE`** (`plib_xlcdc.c` `VIDPRI(0)`), so an
  overlay on OVR1/OVR2 draws on top of the video edges.
- **The open nav drawer covers the video's left edge.** The frame must sit *below*
  the nav so the drawer hides it — so **nav moves OVR1 → OVR2** and the **frame
  takes OVR1** (above HEO, below nav). User-directed.
- **ARGB_4444 chosen** (16 alpha levels → smooth AA at half the bandwidth of 8888;
  1-bit `ARGB_1555` can't AA). The **GFX canvas framework has no 4444 mode**
  (`gfxColorMode` only offers RGBA_5551/8888), so the frame is a **direct-driven
  layer** (own framebuffer + XLCDC PLIB), splash/HEO-style — not a canvas.
- Dashboard behind the video is black (`SCHEME_BACKGROUND` base `0x000000`), so the
  corner-cut fills opaque black and blends seamlessly.

## Approach

### 1. Layer reshuffle: nav OVR1 → OVR2 (frees OVR1 for the frame)
Nav's canvas is RGB565 but it binds via raw `gfxcSetLayer` and never pokes RGBMODE;
today it rode the reveal-time OVR1→RGB565 poke. On OVR2 (which album-art leaves in
RGBA8888) it must set its mode on every open. Reuse the existing `bind_canvas`
(does setLayer + show + RGBMODE poke):
- `ui_manager.c`: add thin verbs `UiManager_ShowNavLayer()` → `bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAVIGATION,
  HW_OVR2, RGB565, true)` and `UiManager_HideNavLayer()` → `gfxcHideCanvas` + update.
- `screen_navigation.c`: `navigation_open` calls `UiManager_ShowNavLayer()` then
  `navigation_slide_to(0)` (replaces the direct `gfxcSetLayer(HW_OVR1)`/`gfxcShowCanvas`);
  `navigation_fx_done` calls `UiManager_HideNavLayer()` (replaces `gfxcHideCanvas`).
  Slide/gating/timing unchanged.
- Remove the now-moot reveal-time OVR1 RGB565 poke (`ui_manager.c` ~L611); OVR1's
  users now self-poke (frame ARGB_4444, song-select dialog RGB565).
- Song-select still uses OVR1 (dialog) + OVR2 (album art). Mutual-exclusion holds:
  nav (OVR2) ⇎ album art (OVR2), frame (OVR1) ⇎ dialog (OVR1) — and the frame is
  hidden whenever video is hidden, so no live conflict. (Same "nav and song-select
  not both open" assumption as today, just shifted to OVR2 — verify on hardware.)

### 2. Video frame overlay — direct-driven ARGB_4444 on OVR1
- **Buffer** (in `screen_video.c`): `static` ARGB_4444, sized to the windowed video
  rect `SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_W × H` (720×480 = 691 KB), `.region_nocache`, 32-byte
  aligned (LCDC DMA reads it; same policy as the dashboard fb).
- **Fill once** at `ScreenVideo_Setup()` via a rounded-rect signed-distance field
  (iq rounded-box SDF, float, computed once). Per pixel, by distance `d` to the
  rounded-rect boundary (radius 6):
  - `d > +½`  → **corner cut**: opaque black `0xF000`.
  - `−½…+½`   → AA blend black↔stroke (both opaque; colour lerp).
  - `−T…−½`   → **stroke**: opaque `0x404040` → `0xF444` (T = 1px).
  - `−T−½…−T` → AA blend stroke↔transparent (**alpha ramp** `0xF→0` — this is the
    edge that smooths the video's rounded corner).
  - `< −T−½`  → transparent `0x0000` (video shows).
- **Register control in `ui_manager.c`** (compositor owns all XLCDC writes):
  - `UiManager_VideoOverlayShow(const void *buf, x, y, w, h)`: drive OVR1 — disable,
    RGBMODE `ARGB_4444`, address = buf, XSTRIDE 0, window (x,y), size (w,h), enable.
  - `UiManager_VideoOverlayHide()`: `XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(OVR1, false)`.
  - Precedent: splash drives its OVR layer directly via PLIB; OVR1 is time-shared
    with the song-select dialog canvas (frame hidden before the dialog opens).

### 3. Frame lifecycle = "windowed video visible on the dashboard" (`screen_video`)
- `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()` → `UiManager_VideoOverlayShow(buf, SCREEN_VIDEO_WIN_*)`.
- `enter_fullscreen()` → `UiManager_VideoOverlayHide()` (edge-to-edge; no frame).
- `UiManager_OpenSongSelect()` (video hidden) → `UiManager_VideoOverlayHide()`
  (close calls `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`, which re-shows it).

## Constants
`SCREEN_VIDEO_BORDER_RADIUS 6`, `_STROKE 1`, colour `0x404040`, cut black, AA over a
1px band. All in `screen_video.c`.

## Files
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.{c,h}` — frame buffer,
  SDF/AA fill, show/hide calls.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.{c,h}` — `UiManager_VideoOverlayShow/Hide`,
  `UiManager_ShowNavLayer/HideNavLayer`; drop OVR1 reveal poke; hide overlay in
  `OpenSongSelect`.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/navigation/screen_navigation.c` — use the
  nav-layer verbs (OVR2).
- Docs: `journal.md` + `ui_compositor.md` (§4 layer table now OVR2=nav, OVR1=frame/
  dialog; new subsection for the frame overlay).

## Notes / risks
- **Bandwidth:** an always-on full-rect OVR1 read while windowed (~720×480 ARGB_4444
  ≈ 41 MB/s) on top of BASE+HEO. Given CSI-2 D-PHY sensitivity to GFX bursts, watch
  for capture stalls on hardware; ARGB_4444 (vs 8888) already halves it.
- Corner-cut assumes solid black behind the video (true today); a patterned
  backdrop there would need a different fill.

## Verification
- Build in MPLAB (no cross-toolchain in-sandbox).
- On hardware: windowed dashboard video shows a 1px `0x404040` frame with smooth
  rounded corners (no jaggies, no square video corners poking through). Open nav →
  drawer slides over and **covers the frame's left edge** (frame is below nav).
  Enter fullscreen → frame gone, edge-to-edge. Open song-select → video+frame gone,
  dialog+album-art render normally; close → frame returns. Confirm no new capture
  stalls in the log (`VIDEO: capture stalled…`).

```

```text
127	static void navigation_open(void)
128	{
129	    /* The drawer's surface is painted once at boot and never changes on show/hide,
130	     * so open is a pure layer bind + slide — no repaint. Grab OVR1 only while shown
131	     * (it and the song-select dialog share OVR1, so the drawer is unbound when
132	     * closed). gfxcSetLayer needs the canvas hidden — it is, until gfxcShowCanvas
133	     * below. Caller ensures the dialog isn't holding OVR1. */
134	    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_NAVIGATION, HW_OVR1);
135	    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_NAVIGATION);
136	    navigation_slide_to(0);
137	    /* Modal: gate the dashboard beneath so nothing behind the drawer reacts. The
138	     * drawer (on OVR1) covers the hamburger, so close is via the drawer's Dashboard
139	     * entry, not the hamburger — gating the dashboard loses no affordance. */
140	    UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(false);
141	    s_navigation_open = true;
142	}
143	
144	static void navigation_close(void)
145	{
146	    /* Slide out to NAVIGATION_CLOSED_X (off-screen), then navigation_fx_done
147	     * disables the layer. NAVIGATION_CLOSED_X avoids the -NAVIGATION_W window-clip
148	     * row-wrap (see its definition); the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch,
149	     * so the final frame is displayed before the hide lands — keeping it in-bounds
150	     * makes that frame a harmless edge sliver instead of the panel's left columns. */
151	    navigation_slide_to(NAVIGATION_CLOSED_X);
152	    s_navigation_open = false;
153	    /* Dashboard input is re-armed by navigation_fx_done once the slide completes,
154	     * NOT here: the drawer still owns OVR1 mid-slide, so re-arming now would let a
155	     * header tap open the song-select modal (which grabs OVR1) before fx_done hides
156	     * the drawer's canvas — the hide would then turn OVR1 off under the dialog. */
157	}
158	
159	/* Move-effect completion callback. At the off-screen end of a close slide the
160	 * window clip leaves a degenerate sliver of the drawer composited at screen
161	 * left; hiding the canvas (disabling its layer) once the slide finishes removes it cleanly. Only
162	 * acts on a completed close — an open leaves the layer shown, and a re-open
163	 * mid-close restarts the move (so this won't fire for the abandoned close).
164	 * Re-arming dashboard input happens here too, only after OVR1 is freed, so no
165	 * mid-slide tap can open a modal onto the layer this hide is about to disable. */
166	static void navigation_fx_done(unsigned int canvasID, GFXC_FX_TYPE effect,
167	                               GFXC_FX_STATUS status, void *parm)
168	{
169	    (void)canvasID;
170	    (void)parm;
171	
172	    if (effect == GFXC_FX_MOVE && status == GFXC_FX_DONE && !s_navigation_open)
173	    {
174	        gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_NAVIGATION);
175	        gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_NAVIGATION);
176	        UiManager_SetDashboardPickable(true);
177	    }
178	}
```

## Implemented (code-complete, pending hardware test)

**The frame** — a 1px rounded frame (`0x404040`, radius 6) with AA corners around the windowed video, as an **ARGB_4444 overlay on OVR1 above HEO**. Since the video is on HEO (not a canvas) and the canvas framework has no 4444 mode, it's a direct-driven layer (splash/HEO-style): a static `.region_nocache` buffer filled once from a rounded-rect SDF (opaque-black corner-cut, 1px stroke, transparent interior; alpha AA on the stroke→video edge). [screen_video.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/video/screen_video.c)

**The layer reshuffle** you called for — **nav OVR1 → OVR2**, so the drawer sits above the frame and covers its left edge when open (z-order `OVR2 > OVR1 > HEO > BASE`):
- New `ui_manager` verbs: `UiManager_VideoOverlayShow/Hide` (OVR1) and `UiManager_ShowNavLayer/HideNavLayer` (nav via `bind_canvas`, which re-pokes RGB565 each open since album-art leaves OVR2 in RGBA8888). [ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c)
- [screen_navigation.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/navigation/screen_navigation.c) uses those verbs; slide/gating/timing unchanged.
- Dropped the now-moot reveal-time OVR1 poke (OVR1 users self-poke).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 17:17:51Z)**_

Noted in both the design doc ([`ui_compositor.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/ui_compositor.md) §16.1) and the journal — not in source, per the repo's "current code only" comment rule.

The gist captured for when we build it:
- **This OVR1 overlay is the home for a per-frame gameplay HUD** (note markers, hit/miss, detected-note boxes) over the video.
- **Direct buffer raster, no Legato** — the canvas framework can't own the layer (no ARGB_4444 mode) and per-frame Legato repaint is too heavy. Fast/minimal overhead → incremental redraw, not full clears.
- **Double-buffer + vsync address flip** to avoid tearing (single buffer was fine only because the frame is static; a per-frame HUD needs two, mirroring the HEO ring's `heo_frame_latch` non-blocking address update).
- **Geometry**: HUD coords map to the *displayed* window, so any source-pixel-derived positions must run through the §15 active-area crop+scale.

One clarification for the record: I wrote it against **OVR1** (the video overlay layer) rather than OVR2 — the frame/HUD overlay sits on OVR1 (above HEO, below the nav on OVR2). That keeps it above the video and below the drawer, which is what a gameplay HUD wants.

Want me to commit now (the four feature files + docs, leaving MCC autosave/specstory out)?

```bash
interior; alpha AA on the stroke->video edge).

left edge, so the frame must sit below nav: move nav OVR1->OVR2, frame
takes OVR1. New ui_manager verbs UiManager_VideoOverlayShow/Hide (OVR1)
and UiManager_ShowNavLayer/HideNavLayer (nav via bind_canvas, re-poking
RGB565 each open since album-art leaves OVR2 in RGBA8888). Drop the

visible; hidden on fullscreen enter and song-select open.

Doc note (ui_compositor.md 16.1): this OVR1 overlay is also the home for
a future per-frame gameplay HUD (direct buffer raster, double-buffered,
minimal overhead).
```

The ISC runs in **RLP BYPASS** ([isc_capture.c:97](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/isc_capture.c#L97)) — so its CBC/gamma stages (though "enabled" in the config struct) are bypassed; nothing expands range there. And the HEO has CBHS (contrast/brightness/hue/sat) + a YCbCr→RGB CSC, both currently zeroed/disabled. The open question is whether HEO CBHS/gamma operates on **RGB** input (`YCCEN=0`) or only YCbCr. Let me confirm against Microchip's docs rather than guess.

## What this actually says
- **Whites cap at ~233**, never reaching 255 — a limited-range *white* ceiling (≈235).
- **Blacks already reach 0** in content (15.6% of pixels ≤16, true 0 present) — so the black end is *not* compressed.

So it's **not** the classic washed-out 16–235 case. Blacks are already good; only the top ~8% of the white range is unused. The grey-pedestal thing I worried about earlier was the **dead border** (~13), and the active-area crop already removes that from the display. So the real-world payoff of expansion is modest: a ~1.09× gain to lift 233→255 (slightly punchier whites), not a dramatic contrast rescue.

## On the "did we / can the HEO do it" question
- **We never expand** — ISC runs RLP **BYPASS** (its CBC/gamma are out of the path), and the HEO is RGB with CBHS/CSC/gamma all disabled. Source passes through untouched.
- **HEO CBHS** — the obvious "limited-range black-level + contrast" block — is per the datasheet **"for YCbCr format purposes."** Our HEO input is RGB888 (`YCCEN=0`), so **it doesn't apply** to our path.
- **HEO gamma** *does* apply to RGB: four 256-entry per-component CLUTs (`GAM=1`). That's the correct tool if we want any RGB remap — **display-only** (detector/gameplay read DDR, unaffected), **zero runtime cost** (LUT at scanout), one-time CLUT load at bring-up.

## Recommendation
**Low priority.** The content is effectively ~0–233, so blacks are fine and the only gain is ~8% brighter whites. If you want a touch more pop it's cheap and low-risk: load the HEO gamma CLUT with a gentle contrast curve (≈1.09× gain, black offset 0, optional mild gamma), enable `GAM`, done — and trivially A/B-toggleable. But I'd **verify on the actual LVDS panel first**: 233 whites may look perfectly fine, and over-gaining risks clipping highlights for no real benefit. The bigger historical concern (grey border pedestal) is already solved by the active-area crop.

## Reconciling the two measurements
- **The ~13 you remember was the dead border** (its *brightest* pixel; mean ~6). That's a real pedestal — and it's cropped out of the display now.
- **Inside the content**, blacks are *not* pinned at 13 — but they're not a clean 0 either. The dark-pixel population **clusters at ~5** (median 8), with a smaller tail of true 0s. - Whites still cap **~233**.

## Revised take
The signal is roughly **~5 → 233** where it "should" be **0 → 255**. That's a real, if gentle, compression on *both* ends:
- black offset ≈ 5 (deepen the near-black cluster to true black)
- gain ≈ 255/(233−5) ≈ **1.12** (lift whites and stretch)

Not dramatic, but more than the "blacks are already fine" I said — pulling the ~5 pedestal down to 0 is the part people actually notice (blacks look properly black instead of dark-grey), and it's exactly what a levels expansion fixes.

## Mechanism (unchanged conclusion)
Do it in the **HEO gamma CLUT** (per-channel RGB LUT, `GAM=1`): load `out = clamp((in − 5) × 1.12)` (optionally with a mild gamma). CBHS's built-in limited-range black-level would be the "right" block but it's **YCbCr-only**, so the RGB gamma-CLUT is our path. Display-only (detector/DDR untouched), zero runtime cost, one-time load, trivially A/B-toggleable.

**Bumping my recommendation from "low" to "worth doing"** — the black-pedestal removal is the meaningful part. _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 17:42:55Z)**_

Done — a single-file change plus docs.

## What I implemented ([ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c))

- **`heo_gamma_load()`** — fills the HEO per-component gamma CLUT (`LCDC_HEOCLUT[256]`, R/G/B each) with a linear levels-expansion curve: `out = clamp((in − 5) × 255 / 228)`, i.e. `VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK=5` → 0 and `VIDEO_LEVELS_WHITE=233` → 255. Called once in `UiManager_Initialize` (while `GAM`/`CLUTEN` are clear, as the datasheet requires for CLUT writes).
- **`GAM` re-assert in `heo_bind`** — since `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode` rewrites `HEOCFG1` with `GAM(0)` on every bind, I re-OR the `GAM` bit right after it so the levels curve stays active across every (re)bind/rebind.

Properties, as you wanted:
- **Fixed** curve, no runtime knob (constants only).
- **Display-only** — the DDR capture is untouched, so the detector/gameplay still see raw pixels; expansion happens in the LCDC at scanout, **zero runtime cost**.
- **RGB path** — used the gamma CLUT because HEO's CBHS limited-range block is YCbCr-only.

Docs updated (journal + `ui_compositor.md` §15.1), and I explicitly corrected my earlier "blacks are already at 0" claim in the journal so the record is right.

Two things for the hardware test:
- **Eyeball it on the LVDS panel** — the ~5/233 pedestal/ceiling came from the screenshot corpus; the real values may differ on your Wii/converter. `VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK`/`WHITE` are the two constants to nudge.
- If it looks over-contrasty or crushes near-blacks, raise `BLACK` toward 0 or lower `WHITE`'s aggressiveness; it's a one-line tweak.

Want me to commit (this file + the two docs, MCC autosave/specstory excluded as usual)?

```text
607	        console_printf("qspi verify: %s (see log)", vok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");

609	    }

629	        return;
630	    }
631	    if (strcmp(sub, "save") == 0)
632	    {
633	        console_printf("settings save: %s", Settings_Save() ? "ok" : "FAIL");
634	        return;
635	    }
636	    if (strcmp(sub, "wipe") == 0)
637	    {
638	        console_printf("settings wipe: %s", Settings_Wipe() ? "ok" : "FAIL");
639	        return;
640	    }
641	    if (strcmp(sub, "stress") == 0)
642	    {
643	        uint32_t n = parse_u32(embeddedCliGetToken(args, 2), 200u);
644	        console_printf("settings stress: %s (see log)", Settings_Stress(n) ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
645	        return;
646	    }
647	    console_printf("usage: settings [dump|save|wipe|stress [n]]  (set backlight via `backlight <pct>`)");
648	}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 17:47:50Z)**_

Added a `gamma` console command for live A/B:

- **`gamma on` / `gamma off`** — toggles the levels expansion; `gamma` with no arg prints the current state.
- Backed by `UiManager_SetVideoLevels(bool)` / `UiManager_GetVideoLevels()`: sets a runtime flag and requests a rebind, so `heo_bind` re-applies (`GAM` on) or bypasses (`GAM` off, raw pass-through) within a frame. Defaults **on**.

Files: [ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c) (flag + gated `GAM` in `heo_bind` + setter/getter), [ui_manager.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.h), [console.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/console/console.c) (`cmd_gamma` + binding), journal note.

Now on the panel you can flip `gamma off`/`gamma on` back-to-back to judge whether the expansion is actually helping — which should make the "hard to tell" much easier to call. If it clearly helps, keep it; if it's marginal or crushes near-blacks, we lower `VIDEO_LEVELS_BLACK` toward 0 (or drop the whole thing).

Want me to commit these (ui_manager.c/.h, console.c, journal, ui_compositor.md — the color-expansion + toggle work), MCC autosave/specstory excluded as usual?

Commit video levels expansion + gamma toggle

```bash
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
marvin: expand video levels via HEO gamma CLUT (+ gamma toggle cmd)

The captured source is mildly range-compressed vs the panel's full
0..255 (corpus: black cluster ~5, white ceiling ~233). The HEO CBHS
limited-range block is YCbCr-only, but the per-component gamma CLUT works
on true RGB, so load it once with a linear levels-expansion curve
(out = clamp((in-5)*255/228)) and enable GAM. Display-only (DDR capture
untouched, so the detector/gameplay see raw pixels), free at scanout.

CLUT is loaded in UiManager_Initialize while GAM/CLUTEN are clear;
XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode rewrites HEOCFG1 with GAM(0) each bind, so
heo_bind re-asserts (or clears) GAM per the s_video_levels flag.

Add a `gamma <on|off>` console command (UiManager_SetVideoLevels) to
toggle the expansion live for A/B comparison on the panel. Confirmed a
clear visible improvement on hardware.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -5
```
